考试写法：NFC is an extension of RFID that supports bi-directional communication; compared with Bluetooth it has lower power consumption and a faster connection speed.

ex.q: Why do some people keep bank cards in RFID-blocking card holders?
ex.a:
1. RFID tags can be read wirelessly from a few metres away.
2. A criminal could steal card data without touching the card.
3. The holder blocks the radio waves.
ex.az:
1. RFID 可在数米外被无线读取。
2. 可能被人偷取资料。
3. 卡套阻挡无线电波。

ex.q: Ada wants smart light bulbs and door sensors that run for a long time on small batteries. Which standard suits them?
ex.a:
1. Zigbee.
2. It is designed for low-powered devices and is used to connect smart home IoT devices.
ex.az:
1. Zigbee。
2. 专为低耗电 IoT 设备设计。

ex.q: A student says: "NFC is one-way like RFID, so phones can only read tags." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: NFC supports bi-directional communication.
2. That is why two phones can exchange files and a phone can make payments.
ex.az:
1. 错误：NFC 支援双向通讯。
2. 所以手机之间可互传文件及付款。

cards.en:
Analogy: a highway. Bandwidth = number of lanes (the most cars possible). Throughput = cars that actually get through (less in a traffic jam). Latency = how long one car takes to arrive.

  • Bandwidth: the maximum data transfer rate, in bps.
  • Throughput: the actual amount of data successfully transferred in a given time. Lower than bandwidth because of poor signals, bandwidth bottlenecks and network congestion.
  • Latency: the delay for data to travel from sender to receiver, in milliseconds (ms). Matters for gaming and video calls.

5G and Wi-Fi 6: give high throughput, low latency and high capacity (more users/devices at once, good for IoT).

Transfer time formula: time (s) = file size (bits) ÷ rate (bps). Always convert bytes to bits first (× 8).

Exam wording: Throughput is the actual amount of data transferred successfully in a given time; it is lower than bandwidth due to network congestion, bottlenecks and poor signals. 5G provides high throughput, low latency and high capacity.
cards.zh:
比喻：高速公路。Bandwidth = 行车线数目（最多能过多少车）；Throughput = 实际通过的车（塞车时较少）；Latency = 一部车到达要多久。

  • Bandwidth（带宽）：最高传输速率，单位 bps。
  • Throughput（吞吐量）：一段时间内实际成功传送的数据量；因讯号差、带宽瓶颈、网络挤塞而低于带宽。
  • Latency（延迟）：数据由发送到接收的延误时间，单位 ms，对游戏和视像通话很重要。

5G 和 Wi-Fi 6：高吞吐量、低延迟、高容量（可同时连更多用户和设备，适合 IoT）。

传输时间公式：时间（秒）= 文件大小（bits）÷ 速率（bps），先把 byte ×8 变成 bit。

考试写法：Throughput is the actual amount of data transferred successfully in a given time; it is lower than bandwidth due to network congestion, bottlenecks and poor signals. 5G provides high throughput, low latency and high capacity.

ex.q: A 500 MB video is downloaded on a 100 Mbps line. Find the minimum download time.
ex.a:
1. Convert to bits: 500 MB × 8 = 4000 Mb.
2. Time = 4000 ÷ 100 = 40 s.

ex.q: The same download actually takes 66.7 s. What is the throughput, and why is it lower than the bandwidth?
ex.a:
1. Throughput = 4000 Mb ÷ 66.7 s ≈ 60 Mbps.
2. Lower than 100 Mbps because of network congestion, bandwidth bottlenecks or poor signal.
ex.az:
1. 4000 ÷ 66.7 ≈ 60 Mbps。
2. 因网络挤塞、瓶颈、讯号差而低于带宽。

ex.q: A student calculates: 500 MB ÷ 100 Mbps = 5 s. What went wrong?
ex.a:
1. Mistake: MB (megabytes) and Mbps (megabits per second) were mixed.
2. Fix: 500 MB × 8 = 4000 Mb, then 4000 ÷ 100 = 40 s.
ex.az:
1. 错误：混淆 MB（byte）和 Mbps（bit）。
2. 先 ×8：4000 Mb ÷ 100 = 40 秒。

demo.src:
size_mb = 500
bandwidth = 100
throughput = 60
bits = size_mb * 8
print("Size in megabits:", bits)
print("Best case:", bits / bandwidth, "s")
print("Real case:", round(bits / throughput, 1), "s")

code.src:
size_mb = 500
bandwidth = 100
throughput = 60
bits = size_mb * 8
print("Size in megabits:", bits)
print("Best case:", bits / bandwidth, "s")
print("Real case:", round(bits / throughput, 1), "s")

notes.t: Bandwidth = maximum rate, 100 megabits per second.
Convert bytes to bits: 1 byte = 8 bits, so 500 MB = 4000 Mb.
Best case time = bits ÷ bandwidth = 40 s.
notes.tz: 理想时间 = bits ÷ 带宽 = 40 秒。

notes.t: Real time = bits ÷ throughput, rounded to 1 decimal place = 66.7 s.
notes.tz: 实际时间 = bits ÷ 吞吐量，四舍五入 1 位 = 66.7 秒。

code.out:
Size in megabits: 4000
Best case: 40.0 s
Real case: 66.7 s

cards.tz: 有线网络 vs 无线网络
cards.en:
Plain idea: cables are faster and safer; wireless is free to move around and easier to set up.

Wired networkWireless network
Common devicesEthernet NIC, switch, UTP cableWireless NIC, access point / wireless router
AdvantagesFaster speed; better data securityNo cabling; easier to set up (flexible location)
DisadvantagesLower mobility (plan long-term needs before setup)Slower; limited transmission distance; less stable; lower security

Factors that slow wireless: distance, obstacles, interference (e.g. a neighbour's Wi-Fi), weather, antenna direction.

Printer by USB vs Wi-Fi: USB → higher data rate, better security, less interference (stable). Wi-Fi → higher mobility, easier to share.

Exam wording: A wired network has a higher data transfer rate and better security; a wireless network needs no cabling and allows mobility, but is slower and less stable.
cards.zh:
简单理解：有线较快较安全；无线可自由移动、较易安装。

有线网络无线网络
常见设备Ethernet NIC、switch、UTP 线无线 NIC、access point／无线路由器
优点速度较快；数据保安较好毋须布线；易安装（位置灵活）
缺点移动性低（安装前要考虑长远需要）较慢；传输距离有限；较不稳定；保安较低

令无线变慢的因素：距离、障碍物、干扰（如邻居 Wi-Fi）、天气、天线方向。

打印机用 USB 或 Wi-Fi：USB → 数据率高、保安好、干扰少（稳定）；Wi-Fi → 移动性高、易共享。

考试写法：A wired network has a higher data transfer rate and better security; a wireless network needs no cabling and allows mobility, but is slower and less stable.

ex.q: All floors have Wi-Fi, but staff still plug laptops in with UTP cables. Give two reasons.
ex.a:
1. A wired network has a higher data transfer rate.
2. The environment may cause interference that disrupts wireless transmission; wired is more stable.
ex.az:
1. 有线数据率较高。
2. 环境干扰会影响无线，有线较稳定。

ex.q: Why do smart home appliances usually support wireless connection?
ex.a:
1. It is easier to install and remove them: no cabling.
2. They can be placed in flexible locations.
ex.az:
1. 安装和移除更容易，不用布线。
2. 位置灵活。

ex.q: A student says: "A wireless LAN increases the data transmission speed of the school network." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: wireless is usually slower than wired.
2. Real benefits: more devices without adding switches, and connecting from anywhere (e.g. playground).
ex.az:
1. 错误：无线通常较慢。
2. 真正好处：不用加 switch 也能连更多设备，并可在任何地方连线。

cards.tz: 互联网服务供应商与宽频
cards.en:
Analogy: an ISP is like the water company: it owns the big pipes and charges you to connect your flat.

ISP (Internet Service Provider): a company that provides services for accessing the Internet (e.g. home broadband companies, mobile networks).

Four common access methods: broadband, leased line, mobile data, Wi-Fi hotspot.

Broadband: a wired, always-on connection through:

  • ADSL: copper telephone line all the way (slowest);
  • FTTC (Fibre To The Cabinet): fibre to a street cabinet, copper phone line to the home;
  • Fibre: e.g. FTTH (Fibre To The Home), fibre runs right into the flat.

The ISP's network is shared with other users, so speed can drop at busy times. Bandwidth high, cost moderate, security high, availability high: the usual choice for homes.

Exam wording: An ISP is a company that provides services for accessing the Internet. Broadband is a wired connection with high bandwidth and moderate cost, but the bandwidth is shared with other users.
cards.zh:
比喻：ISP 像水务公司：拥有大水管，收费让你的单位接驳。

ISP（Internet Service Provider）：提供上网服务的公司（家居宽带公司、流动网络商）。

四种常见上网方式：broadband、leased line、mobile data、Wi-Fi hotspot。

Broadband（宽带）：有线、长期在线，经：

  • ADSL：全程铜电话线（最慢）；
  • FTTC（Fibre To The Cabinet）：光纤到街边机柜，再用铜电话线入户；
  • 光纤：如 FTTH（Fibre To The Home），光纤直入住户。

ISP 网络与其他用户共用，繁忙时间可能变慢。带宽高、成本中等、保安高、可用性高，是家庭常用选择。

考试写法：An ISP is a company that provides services for accessing the Internet. Broadband is a wired connection with high bandwidth and moderate cost, but the bandwidth is shared with other users.

ex.q: A family wants Internet at home for streaming and homework at a reasonable price. Which access method? Why?
ex.a:
1. Fixed location, needs high bandwidth, moderate budget.
2. Answer: broadband (e.g. FTTH): high bandwidth at moderate cost, high availability.
ex.az:
1. 固定地点、要高带宽、预算中等。
2. 宽带（如 FTTH）：带宽高、成本适中。

ex.q: Home broadband is fast at 10 am but slow at 9 pm. Explain.
ex.a:
1. Broadband bandwidth on the ISP's network is shared with other users.
2. At 9 pm many neighbours stream → congestion → lower throughput.
ex.az:
1. 宽带与其他用户共用。
2. 晚上多人串流 → 挤塞 → 变慢。

ex.q: A student writes: "An ISP is the router in my home." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: confusing a device with a company.
2. Correct: an ISP is a company that provides Internet access services; the router is your own device that connects to the ISP.
ex.az:
1. 错误：把设备当公司。
2. 正确：ISP 是提供上网服务的公司；router 是家中连接 ISP 的设备。

cards.en:
Plain idea: broadband speed depends on how much of the path from the ISP to your home is fibre instead of copper.

Broadband = high-speed wired Internet access; its wide bandwidth can carry multiple signals at the same time.

TypeISP exchange → cabinetCabinet → homeDownload speed
ADSLCopper telephone cableCopper telephone cableLowest
FTTC (Fibre-to-the-cabinet)Fibre opticCopper telephone cableModerate
FTTH (Fibre-to-the-home)Fibre opticFibre opticFastest

There are also satellite and microwave broadband, which link subscribers to the ISP by radio waves.

Changing from ADSL to FTTH: besides cables, the modem must change (ADSL modem → fibre optic modem / ONT).

Exam wording: FTTH uses fibre optic cable all the way to the home, so it is faster than FTTC and ADSL, which use copper telephone cable for part or all of the path.
cards.zh:
简单理解：宽带速度取决于由 ISP 到你家的路径有多少是光纤而不是铜线。

Broadband（宽带）＝高速有线上网；带宽阔，可同时传送多个讯号。

类型ISP 机楼 → 机柜机柜 → 住户下载速度
ADSL铜电话线铜电话线最慢
FTTC（光纤到机柜）光纤铜电话线中等
FTTH（光纤到户）光纤光纤最快

亦有用无线电波连接 ISP 的卫星及微波宽带。

由 ADSL 转 FTTH：除线缆外，modem 也要更换（ADSL modem → 光纤 modem／ONT）。

考试写法：FTTH uses fibre optic cable all the way to the home, so it is faster than FTTC and ADSL, which use copper telephone cable for part or all of the path.

ex.q: Rank ADSL, FTTC and FTTH by download speed and explain.
ex.a:
1. FTTH > FTTC > ADSL.
2. FTTH is fibre all the way; FTTC uses copper from the cabinet to the home; ADSL is copper all the way.
3. More fibre → faster.
ex.az:
1. FTTH > FTTC > ADSL。
2. 光纤越多越快。

ex.q: Dave changes from ADSL to FTTH. Besides the cables, what hardware must change?
ex.a:
1. The modem.
2. An ADSL modem works with copper phone lines; FTTH needs a fibre optic modem (ONT) that converts light signals and electrical signals.
ex.az:
1. Modem。
2. 要换成光纤 modem（ONT）。

ex.q: A student says: "FTTC means fibre goes right into the flat." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: that is FTTH.
2. FTTC = fibre to the cabinet; the last part to the home is still copper telephone cable.
ex.az:
1. 错误：那是 FTTH。
2. FTTC 光纤只到机柜，最后一段仍是铜线。

cards.en:
Analogy: broadband is like a public road you share with everyone. A leased line is your own private road straight to the ISP: no traffic from others, but very expensive.

Leased line: a private, dedicated channel connecting directly to the ISP that does not share bandwidth with other users.

  • Highest bandwidth (guaranteed, often symmetric).
  • Highest security (private channel).
  • More stable: no congestion from other users.
  • Highest cost; availability moderate (must be installed to the site).

Used by banks, large companies, data centres, and to link company branches.

Exam wording: A leased line is a private network connecting to the ISP directly over a dedicated channel which does not share bandwidth with other users. It has the highest bandwidth, security and stability but the highest cost.
cards.zh:
比喻：宽带像和大家共用的公路；leased line 是直通 ISP 的私家路：没有别人塞车，但非常贵。

Leased line（专线）：直接连接 ISP 的私人专用通道，不与其他用户共用带宽。

  • 带宽最高（有保证，通常上下对称）。
  • 保安最高（私人通道）。
  • 更稳定：没有别人造成的挤塞。
  • 成本最高；可用性中等（要专门铺设到地点）。

用于银行、大公司、数据中心，及连接公司分行。

考试写法：A leased line is a private network connecting to the ISP directly over a dedicated channel which does not share bandwidth with other users. It has the highest bandwidth, security and stability but the highest cost.

ex.q: A bank must link its 20 branches to head office for real-time transactions. Broadband or leased line? Give TWO reasons.
ex.a:
1. Sensitive money data, must never slow down.
2. Answer: leased line.
3. Reasons: highest security (dedicated private channel); stable, guaranteed bandwidth not shared with others.
ex.az:
1. 敏感、不能慢 → 专线。
2. 私人通道最安全；带宽有保证、不与人共用、稳定。

ex.q: Why wouldn't a normal family choose a leased line?
ex.a:
1. A family does not need guaranteed bandwidth or bank-level security.
2. A leased line has the highest cost.
Answer: too expensive for their needs; broadband is good enough.
ex.az:
1. 家庭不需要保证带宽和银行级保安。
2. 专线最贵 → 宽带已足够。

ex.q: A student writes: "A leased line is faster because it uses wireless." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a leased line is wired.
2. Correct: it is better because its dedicated channel does not share bandwidth with other users.
ex.az:
1. 错误：专线是有线的。
2. 正确：专用通道不与他人共用带宽，所以更好。

frames.en: Many homes share the ISP's local network. At night everyone streams → congestion.
frames.zh: 很多住户共用 ISP 本地网络，晚上大家串流 → 挤塞。

frames.en: The bank has its own channel straight to the ISP core. Nobody else uses it.
frames.zh: 银行有直达 ISP 核心的专用通道，别人不能用。

cards.t: Leased line vs broadband at the same speed
cards.tz: 相同速度下的专线 vs 宽带
cards.en:
The trap: "A 10M leased line is faster than 10M broadband." Not true: they have the same rated data transfer rate (10M).

What a leased line really gives:

  • A dedicated channel that does not share infrastructure with others → fixed (guaranteed) bandwidth.
  • More reliable and stable (no congestion from neighbours).
  • More secure (private network to the ISP).
  • But higher cost than broadband of the same bandwidth.

In the comparison table a leased line has the "Highest" bandwidth because companies usually buy large leased lines, but at the same rated speed the advantages are guarantee, stability and security, not raw speed.

Also: broadband is wired, so it is not normally affected by bad weather either; weather affects satellite and microwave.

Exam wording: A leased line provides a guaranteed bandwidth over a dedicated channel that does not share infrastructure, so it is more reliable, stable and secure, though more expensive.
cards.zh:
陷阱：「10M 专线比 10M 宽带快」——错，两者额定数据传输率相同（10M）。

专线真正的好处：

  • 专用通道，不与他人共用基建 → 固定（有保证）带宽。
  • 更可靠、稳定（不受邻居挤塞影响）。
  • 更安全（连 ISP 的私人网络）。
  • 但相同带宽下成本较高。

比较表中专线带宽列为「最高」，因为公司通常租用大带宽专线；但在相同额定速度下，优点是有保证、稳定和安全，不是更快。

另外宽带是有线，一般不受恶劣天气影响；受天气影响的是卫星和微波。

考试写法：A leased line provides a guaranteed bandwidth over a dedicated channel that does not share infrastructure, so it is more reliable, stable and secure, though more expensive.

ex.q: Why would a company choose a 10M leased line instead of 10M broadband?
ex.a:
1. Bandwidth is guaranteed (dedicated channel, not shared).
2. Connection is more reliable/stable.
3. It is more secure.
ex.az:
1. 带宽有保证。
2. 更稳定可靠。
3. 更安全。

ex.q: Which statement is incorrect: (A) broadband is cheaper than a leased line of the same bandwidth; (B) broadband is interfered by bad weather but leased lines are not; (C) leased lines are more stable and secure; (D) leased lines do not share infrastructure.
ex.a:
1. B is incorrect.
2. Broadband is a wired connection; bad weather mainly affects satellite and microwave links.
ex.az:
1. B 错。
2. 宽带是有线，天气主要影响卫星和微波。

ex.q: A student answers: "The 10M leased line has a higher maximum data transfer rate." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: both are 10M, so the maximum rate is the same.
2. The benefit is guaranteed bandwidth, stability and security.
ex.az:
1. 错误：两者同是 10M。
2. 好处是带宽有保证、稳定、安全。

cards.tz: 流动数据与 Wi-Fi 热点
cards.en:
Analogy: mobile data is like carrying your own water bottle (works anywhere, you pay per litre). A Wi-Fi hotspot is like a free public water fountain (cheap, but only in some places and not always clean).

Mobile data: wireless access through the cellular network (4G/5G). Works almost anywhere with signal.

  • 5G: bandwidth high, cost high, security high, availability high.

Wi-Fi hotspot: wireless access points in public places (malls, cafés, MTR stations).

  • Bandwidth moderate (shared by many).
  • Cost low (often free).
  • Security lowest: anyone can join; data may be unencrypted; fake hotspots may steal data.
  • Availability low: only inside the hotspot area.

Hong Kong fact: over 36 000 free Wi-Fi hotspots (2020) under the Wi-Fi.HK brand, free to use with no registration (public transport, libraries, universities, malls, cafés). A pocket Wi-Fi shares mobile data with travel companions by Wi-Fi.

Exam wording: Mobile data provides wireless Internet access through the cellular network with high availability. A public Wi-Fi hotspot has low cost but the lowest security and low availability.
cards.zh:
比喻：流动数据像自己带水樽（哪里都可以用，按用量付费）；Wi-Fi hotspot 像公共饮水机（便宜，但只在某些地方，也不一定干净）。

Mobile data（流动数据）：经流动电话网络（4G/5G）无线上网，有讯号就能用。

  • 5G：带宽高、成本高、保安高、可用性高。

Wi-Fi hotspot：公共地方的无线接入点（商场、咖啡店、港铁站）。

  • 带宽中等（多人共用）。
  • 成本低（常免费）。
  • 保安最低：谁都能连；数据可能未加密；假 hotspot 可偷资料。
  • 可用性低：只在热点范围内。

香港资料：「Wi-Fi.HK」品牌下有超过 36 000 个免费 Wi-Fi 热点（2020），免费、不用登记（公共交通、图书馆、大学、商场、咖啡店）。Pocket Wi-Fi 可经 Wi-Fi 与同行者共享流动数据。

考试写法：Mobile data provides wireless Internet access through the cellular network with high availability. A public Wi-Fi hotspot has low cost but the lowest security and low availability.

ex.q: A salesperson travels around Hong Kong all day and needs to check email anywhere. Which access method?
ex.a:
1. Moves around → needs high availability.
2. Answer: mobile data (5G); works almost anywhere with cellular signal.
ex.az:
1. 要随处可用。
2. 流动数据（5G）。

ex.q: Give TWO precautions when using a free café Wi-Fi hotspot.
ex.a:
1. Avoid online banking / entering passwords, since data may be unencrypted.
2. Use HTTPS websites or a VPN, and check the hotspot name is the café's real SSID (avoid fake hotspots).
ex.az:
1. 避免网上理财、输入密码。
2. 用 HTTPS 或 VPN，确认是店家真正的 SSID。

ex.q: A student writes: "Public Wi-Fi is safe because it needs a password printed on the wall." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: a password everyone in the café can see does not stop other users or attackers on the same network.
2. Correct: hotspots have the lowest security because anyone can connect.
ex.az:
1. 错误：人人都看得到的密码挡不了同网络的攻击者。

cards.en:
Plain idea: each "G" is a new generation of mobile network. 1G was voice only; each later one added more.

  • 1G: phone calls. 2G: + texts. 3G: + Internet. 4G: + Ultra HD and 3D video. 5G: + smart home / IoT.
2G3G4G5G
Max rate (bandwidth)473 kbps84.4 Mbps1000 Mbps10 Gbps
Technology standardGSMWCDMALTE AdvancedNR

4G vs 5G: 5G has latency below 1 ms (4G about 10 ms), much higher device density (over 1 000 000 devices per km² vs about 100 000), around 10 Gbps vs 1 Gbps, higher reliability and lower power use. So 5G has larger capacity, lower latency and connects many devices at the same time, helping IoT.

Exam wording: Compared with 4G, 5G has a higher data transfer rate, larger capacity and lower latency, and can connect many devices at the same time, which supports IoT.

cards.en:
Analogy: to ask a stranger the time, you both use the same language, you say "Excuse me" first, then you wait for the answer. Those shared rules are a human protocol.

Communication software = a network application on an end device (phone, PC) that lets people talk and share things over a network. Examples: email, instant messaging, web conferencing, the web browser.

  • Why use the Internet to communicate? fast/instant, low cost, can send multimedia (photos, voice, video).
  • Protocol = an agreed set of rules. Every device must follow the same one.
  • Because the rules are a standard, a Windows PC, an iPhone and a Linux server can all talk to each other.

Exam wording: A protocol is a set of rules that specify the format and order of the data sent and received between devices. Standard protocols allow devices with different operating systems/hardware to communicate.
cards.zh:
比喻：你问陌生人时间，双方要用同一种语言、先说“不好意思”、再等对方回答。这些共同规则就是人类的“协定”。

通讯软件 (communication software)：在终端设备上运行、让人经网络沟通和分享资源的应用程式，例如 email、instant messaging、web conferencing、web browser。

  • 好处：快（即时）、便宜、可传多媒体。
  • Protocol（协定）：大家同意的一套规则，所有设备都要遵守同一套。
  • 因为是标准，Windows、iOS、Linux 的设备都能互相通讯。

考试写法：A protocol is a set of rules that specify the format and order of the data sent and received between devices. Standard protocols allow devices with different operating systems to communicate.

ex.q: Why can an iPhone (iOS) open a web page stored on a Linux server?
ex.a:
1. Both devices follow the same standard protocols (TCP/IP, HTTP/HTTPS).
2. A protocol fixes the format and order of the data.
3. So each side understands the other's data, whatever its operating system.
ex.az:
1. 双方都遵守同一套标准协定 (TCP/IP、HTTP)。
2. 协定规定数据的格式与次序。
3. 所以操作系统不同也能互相理解。

ex.q: Give two advantages of using instant messaging instead of posting a letter.
ex.a:
1. Instant: the message arrives in seconds.
2. Lower cost: no stamps; only Internet fee.
(Also: can send photos/voice/video – multimedia.)
ex.az:
1. 即时送达。
2. 成本低。
（亦可传多媒体。）

2. Software (e.g. a browser) follows the protocol.

ex.az:
1. 协定不是程式，是一套规则。
2. 软件（如浏览器）是“遵守”协定。
3. 正确写法见上。

cards.t: Protocols in everyday terms and the TCP 3-way handshake
cards.tz: 协定的日常比喻与 TCP 三次握手
cards.en:
Analogy: asking a stranger the time. You use a shared language and start politely: "Hello" → "Hello" → "What time is it?" → "10:00". Computers follow rules in the same way.

A protocol is a set of rules that specify the format and order of data sent and received. Because everyone follows the same standard, devices with different operating systems can still communicate.

TCP 3-way handshake (how TCP sets up a connection before sending data):

  1. Client → server: connection request.
  2. Server → client: connection response.
  3. Client → server: acknowledgement; then data (e.g. GET /index.html) is sent.

Why use the Internet for communication? Instant/fast, lower cost, supports multimedia messages.

Why split data into packets? If one packet is corrupted, only that packet needs to be sent again, not the whole file.

Exam wording: Protocols are sets of rules that specify the format and order of data exchanged, so devices with different operating systems can communicate.
cards.zh:
比喻：向陌生人问时间：用共同语言、先打招呼：「你好」→「你好」→「几点？」→「10:00」。电脑也一样要守规则。

Protocol（协定）是规定收发数据格式及次序的一套规则。因为大家依同一标准，不同操作系统的设备也能沟通。

TCP 三次握手（3-way handshake）（TCP 传数据前建立连接）：

  1. 客户端 → 服务器：连接请求。
  2. 服务器 → 客户端：连接回应。
  3. 客户端 → 服务器：确认；之后才传数据（如 GET /index.html）。

用互联网沟通的好处：即时、成本低、支援多媒体讯息。

为何分成封包？某封包损坏时，只需重传该封包，不用重传整个文件。

考试写法：Protocols are sets of rules that specify the format and order of data exchanged, so devices with different operating systems can communicate.

ex.q: A Mac and a Windows PC exchange email without problems. Why?
ex.a:
1. Both follow the same standardised communication protocols (e.g. TCP/IP, SMTP).
2. Protocols fix the format and order of data, so the OS does not matter.
ex.az:
1. 两者遵守同一标准协定。
2. 协定规定格式及次序，与操作系统无关。

ex.q: Why is data divided into packets before transmission?
ex.a:
1. If a packet is corrupted, only that packet is resent.
2. Packets can also take different paths to avoid congestion.
ex.az:
1. 损坏只需重传该封包。
2. 封包可走不同路径避开挤塞。

ex.q: A student says: "TCP sends the data first and then says hello." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: order is reversed.
2. TCP first sets up a connection with a 3-way handshake, then sends data.
ex.az:
1. 错误：次序相反。
2. TCP 先三次握手建立连接，再传数据。

cards.en:
Analogy: you post a 500-page book to a friend in 5 numbered boxes. Couriers may take different roads, boxes arrive in any order, and your friend uses the numbers to rebuild the book. If one box is damaged, only that box is sent again.

  • Packet = one small piece of the data, plus labels.
  • TCP (Transmission Control Protocol): splits data into packets, numbers them, checks they arrive, asks again for lost/damaged ones, and reassembles them in order.
  • IP (Internet Protocol): puts the source and destination IP addresses on every packet and routes it (picks a path; can pick another path to avoid congestion = a traffic jam on the network).

4 steps: 1 Data division → 2 Use of IP address → 3 Routing → 4 Reassembling.

Exam wording: TCP divides data into smaller packets, numbers them, and reassembles them at the destination. IP adds source and destination IP addresses and selects the path (an alternative path to avoid congestion). If a packet is corrupted, only that packet needs to be resent.
cards.zh:
比喻：你把一本书分成 5 个有编号的箱子寄给朋友，速递可能走不同路、箱子不按次序到；朋友按编号还原。坏了一个箱只重寄那一个。

  • Packet：数据的一小块，加上标签。
  • TCP：把数据分成 packets、编号、检查有否到达、要求重传遗失/损坏的、最后按次序重组。
  • IP：在每个 packet 加 source 与 destination IP address，并选择路径 (routing)；可走替代路径避开 network congestion（网络塞车）。

四步：Data division → Use of IP address → Routing → Reassembling。

考试写法：TCP divides data into smaller packets, numbers them, and reassembles them at the destination. IP adds source and destination IP addresses and selects the path. If a packet is corrupted, only that packet needs to be resent.

ex.q: A 5-packet message arrives in the order 2,1,5,3,4 and packet 3 is corrupted. What does TCP do?
ex.a:
1. Detects packet 3 is corrupted and asks for only packet 3 again.
2. Waits until all 5 packets are there.
3. Uses the numbers to put them in order 1,2,3,4,5 and rebuilds the message.
ex.az:
1. 只要求重传第 3 个。
2. 等 5 个都到齐。
3. 按编号 1–5 重组。

ex.q: Why can packets of the same email arrive out of order?
ex.a:
1. IP routes each packet separately.
2. Packets may take different paths (e.g. to avoid congestion).
3. Different paths take different times, so arrival order changes.
ex.az:
1. IP 独立为每个 packet 选路。
2. 可能走不同路径。
3. 时间不同，所以次序乱。

ex.q: Student: "IP splits the data into packets and TCP adds the IP addresses." Correct it.
ex.a:
The jobs are swapped.
1. TCP divides into packets, numbers and reassembles.
2. IP adds source/destination IP addresses and routes.
ex.az: 两者职责调转了：TCP 负责分割/编号/重组；IP 负责加地址和选路。

frames.en: TCP splits "HELLO WORLD" into packets #1 #2 #3 and numbers them.
frames.zh: TCP 把数据分成 #1 #2 #3 并编号。

frames.en: IP adds source IP 203.0.113.5 and destination IP 198.51.100.7 to each packet.
frames.zh: IP 在每个 packet 加上来源与目的 IP。

frames.en: Router B is congested, so packet #2 takes the alternative path via Router C. #1 and #3 go via B.
frames.zh: Router B 塞车，#2 改走 Router C。

frames.en: Packets arrive as #3, #1, #2. TCP checks all arrived and sorts them: #1 #2 #3 → "HELLO WORLD".
frames.zh: 到达次序 #3 #1 #2，TCP 按编号重组。

cards.tz: 五层 TCP/IP 协定堆叠与封装
cards.en:
Analogy: sending a gift. You write a card (data), put it in a box with a label (transport), the post office adds the address (network), the local van adds a delivery slip for the next stop (data link), and the van drives on the road (physical). The receiver unwraps in reverse order.

LayerWhat it doesAdds
Applicationinterface between user and app (browser, email client)the data, e.g. "Hello"
Transportdivides data into packets (TCP)transport header (TH)
Networkadds IP addresses, chooses the pathnetwork header (NH)
Data Linkmaps IP address to MAC address; moves frames between two directly connected devicesframe header
Physicalsends bit streams (0s and 1s) over cable/radio–

Encapsulation = adding a header at each layer on the way down. Decapsulation = the receiver removing the headers on the way up and reassembling.

Protocols at each layer: Application: HTTP, SMTP, POP, IMAP, FTP. Transport: TCP / UDP. Network: IP. Data Link: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol, maps IP address → MAC address). Physical: Ethernet / 802.11.

Names of the data unit: Application: data → Transport: segment (TCP header added) → Network: datagram/packet (IP header) → Data Link: frame (MAC header + trailer) → Physical: bits. Encapsulation may add a header and/or a trailer.

Exam wording: Transport layer divides data into packets and adds a transport header; Network layer adds a network header with IP addresses; Data Link layer maps the IP address to the MAC address; Physical layer transmits the data as bit streams. Decapsulation is the reverse process.
cards.zh:
比喻：寄礼物：写卡（数据）→ 装箱贴标签（transport）→ 邮局加地址（network）→ 小货车加下一站派送单（data link）→ 在马路上行驶（physical）。收件人反序拆开。

层作用加上
Application用户与应用程式的介面数据
Transport把数据分成 packetsTH
Network加 IP address、选路径NH
Data Link把 IP 对应到 MAC address，在直接相连设备间传 frameframe header
Physical以 0/1 bit stream 经电缆/无线电传送–

向下逐层加 header = encapsulation（封装）；接收端向上逐层拆除并重组 = decapsulation。

各层协定：应用层：HTTP、SMTP、POP、IMAP、FTP。传输层：TCP／UDP。网络层：IP。数据链路层：ARP（Address Resolution Protocol，把 IP 地址对应到 MAC 地址）。实体层：Ethernet／802.11。

各层数据单位：应用层：data → 传输层：segment（加 TCP header）→ 网络层：datagram／packet（加 IP header）→ 数据链路层：frame（加 MAC header 及 trailer）→ 实体层：bits。封装可加 header 及／或 trailer。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: At which layer is (a) the destination IP address added, (b) the IP address mapped to a MAC address, (c) the data turned into 1s and 0s?
ex.a:
(a) Network layer (network header).
(b) Data Link layer.
(c) Physical layer.
ex.az: (a) Network (b) Data Link (c) Physical。

ex.q: A packet on the cable looks like [frame hdr][NH][TH][Hello]. Which header does the receiver remove first? Why?
ex.a:
1. The receiver goes up the stack: Physical → Data Link → Network → Transport → Application.
2. So the outermost header (frame header, Data Link) is removed first, then NH, then TH.
3. This is decapsulation.
ex.az: 接收端由下而上，先拆最外层 frame header，再 NH、TH，这叫 decapsulation。

ex.q: Student: "The Application layer divides the data into packets." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The Application layer only provides the interface (browser, email).
2. Dividing into packets is the Transport layer (TCP), which adds the transport header.
ex.az: Application 只是介面；分 packets 的是 Transport layer。

demo.title: Encapsulation down the stack, decapsulation up

frames.en: Data: Hello
frames.zh: 数据：Hello

frames.en: Split into packets, add TH: [TH|Hello]
frames.zh: 分 packet，加 TH

frames.en: Add NH with source & destination IP: [NH|TH|Hello]
frames.zh: 加含 IP 的 NH

frames.en: Map IP → MAC of next device, form a frame: [MAC|NH|TH|Hello]
frames.zh: IP 对应 MAC，组成 frame

frames.en: Sent as bits: 0100100001100101…
frames.zh: 以 0/1 传送

frames.en: Receiver goes up: removes MAC header → NH → TH, reassembles packets → app shows Hello.
frames.zh: 接收端向上逐层拆 header、重组 → Hello

cards.en:
Analogy: an IP address is like your home address (changes when you move). A MAC address is like your ID card number (stays with you).

  • IP address: a number that identifies a device on a TCP/IP network. Must be unique in that network. Assigned via ICANN (the body that manages names and numbers) through your ISP.
  • Every packet carries a source IP (sender) and destination IP (receiver), like an envelope.
  • MAC address: 48-bit, burnt into the NIC (network card) by the maker; used inside a local network and for MAC address filtering.
  • Routers forward by IP; switches forward by MAC.
  • Windows: ipconfig shows your IP.

Exam wording: An IP address is a changeable numerical address used to identify a device in a network; it must be unique. The IP address identifies the location of the device in the network, while the MAC address identifies the device (NIC) itself.
cards.zh:
比喻：IP address 像住址（搬家会变）；MAC address 像身份证号码（跟着你）。

  • IP address：在 TCP/IP 网络中识别设备的数字，须唯一；由 ICANN 经 ISP 分配。
  • 每个 packet 有 source IP 与 destination IP。
  • MAC address：48-bit，由制造商写入网卡 (NIC)，可作 MAC address filtering。
  • Router 按 IP 转发；switch 按 MAC。
  • Windows 用 ipconfig 查看 IP。

考试写法：An IP address is a changeable numerical address used to identify a device in a network; it must be unique. IP identifies the location; MAC identifies the device itself.

ex.q: A laptop moves from home Wi-Fi to school Wi-Fi. Which of IP / MAC may change? Why?
ex.a:
1. IP may change: each network assigns it, and it shows location in that network.
2. MAC stays: it is fixed in the NIC by the manufacturer.
ex.az: IP 可能变（由所在网络分配）；MAC 不变（写在网卡）。

ex.q: Two PCs in the same office both get 192.168.1.20. What happens and why?
ex.a:
1. IP addresses must be unique in a network.
2. Packets for 192.168.1.20 cannot reach the right PC → IP conflict; one or both lose connection.
3. Fix: give one PC a different address.
ex.az: IP 须唯一；重复会冲突、连线出问题，要改其中一部。

ex.q: Student: "A switch uses the IP address to send frames to the right port." What's wrong?
ex.a:
1. A switch works in the local network with MAC addresses.
2. It is the router that forwards by IP address between networks.
ex.az: Switch 用 MAC；用 IP 转发的是 router。

cards.en:
Idea: an IPv4 address is 32 bits (0s and 1s). Reading 32 bits is hard, so we cut it into four 8-bit pieces (octets) and write each as a decimal number with dots.

  • Each octet: 8 bits → 0 to 255.
  • Range: 0.0.0.0 – 255.255.255.255.
  • Total: 232 = 4,294,967,296 ≈ 4.3 billion.
  • Valid? exactly 4 parts, each a whole number 0–255.
  • Convert an octet with place values 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1; always write 8 digits.

Example: 148.7.52.1 = 10010100.00000111.00110100.00000001

Exam wording: An IPv4 address is a 32-bit numerical address formed by four 8-bit numbers separated by periods; each number ranges from 0 to 255.
cards.zh:
概念：IPv4 是 32 个 0/1。太难读，于是切成四段各 8 bits（octet），每段写成十进制，用句点分隔。

  • 每个 octet：0–255。
  • 范围 0.0.0.0 – 255.255.255.255。
  • 总数 232 ≈ 43 亿。
  • 有效？刚好 4 段，每段 0–255 整数。
  • 用位值 128 64 32 16 8 4 2 1 转换，每段写满 8 位。

考试写法：An IPv4 address is a 32-bit numerical address formed by four 8-bit numbers separated by periods; each ranges from 0 to 255.

ex.q: Convert 192.168.10.5 to binary.
ex.az: 每段拆成位值之和，补足 8 位。

ex.a:
(a) invalid: 256 > 255.
(b) invalid: only 3 parts.
(c) valid.
(d) invalid: 5 parts.
ex.az: 只有 (c) 有效。

ex.q: Student writes 10 as "1010" inside an IPv4 binary address. Why is it marked wrong?
ex.a:
1. Each octet must be exactly 8 bits.
2. Pad with leading zeros: 10 → 00001010.
3. Otherwise the full address is not 32 bits.
ex.az: 每段必须 8 位，要补前导零：00001010。

cards.t: IPv6 and why it was introduced
cards.en:
Why: 4.3 billion IPv4 addresses sounded huge, but now phones, laptops, watches, smart lights… all need one. IPv4 addresses are running out, so IPv6 was made with far more addresses.

  • 128 bits, written as eight groups of 16 bits, each group = 4 hexadecimal digits (0–9, a–f), separated by colons.
  • Example: 2025:1ab1:abcd:1025:20b5:a19a:a315:1212
  • Total: 2128 ≈ 3.4×1038 = 296 times IPv4.
  • Why hex? 1 hex digit = 4 bits, so 16 bits = 4 hex digits; much shorter than binary.

Exam wording: IPv4 addresses are being used up due to the growth of Internet devices, so IPv6 was introduced to provide more addresses. An IPv6 address is a 128-bit address formed by eight 16-bit hexadecimal numbers separated by colons.
cards.zh:
原因：手机、手表、智能灯泡都要 IP，IPv4 快用完，于是推出地址多得多的 IPv6。

  • 128 bits，分八组各 16 bits，每组 4 位十六进制，以冒号分隔。
  • 例：2025:1ab1:abcd:1025:20b5:a19a:a315:1212
  • 总数 2128，是 IPv4 的 296 倍。
  • 1 位 hex = 4 bits，所以 16 bits = 4 位 hex。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: How many times more addresses does IPv6 have than IPv4?
Convert the IPv6 group a315 to binary.
Student: "IPv6 has 8 groups of 8 bits, so it is 64 bits." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Each IPv6 group is 16 bits (4 hex digits × 4 bits).
2. 8 × 16 = 128 bits.
(8-bit groups belong to IPv4.)
ex.az: 每组是 16 bits，共 128 bits；8-bit 一段是 IPv4。

cards.en:
Why: full IPv6 addresses are long and full of zeros. Two rules make them shorter.

  1. Drop leading zeros in each group: 0db8 → db8, 0f20 → f20, 0000 → 0. (Never drop zeros at the end: f200 stays f200.)
  2. Zero compression: replace one run of consecutive all-zero groups with ::. If there are two runs, compress the longer one.

Why only once? With two "::" you can't tell how many zero groups each one hides.

To expand: count the groups shown; :: = (8 − shown) groups of 0000.

Exam wording: Leading zeros in each group can be omitted. One sequence of consecutive zero groups can be replaced by a double colon (::), and :: can appear only once.
cards.zh:
原因：完整 IPv6 太长又多零，用两条规则简写。

  1. 删前导零：0db8 → db8，0000 → 0（尾部零不可删：f200 不变）。
  2. Zero compression：把一串连续全零组改成 ::；有两串就压缩较长的。

为何只能一次？两个 :: 就无法知道各代表多少组。

还原：:: = (8 − 已显示组数) 组 0000。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.a:
1. Drop leading zeros: 2001:0:0:f20:0:0:0:f10.
2. Zero runs: groups 2–3 (2 groups) and 5–7 (3 groups).
3. Compress the longer: 2001:0:0:f20::f10.
ex.az: 先删前导零，再把较长的三组零改成 ::。

ex.q: Expand fe80::1.
ex.az: 显示 2 组，:: 代表 6 组零。
显示 5 组，:: = 3 组零，并补回前导零。

ex.q: Student writes 2001::f20::f10. Why is it invalid?
ex.a:
1. :: appears twice.
2. 8 − 3 = 5 zero groups are hidden, but we can't tell if it is 2+3, 1+4, 3+2…
3. Only one :: is allowed: 2001:0:0:f20::f10.
ex.az: 出现两次 ::，无法确定各代表几组；只可用一次。

frames.zh: 原地址
删前导零

frames.en: Run A: groups 2–3 (length 2). Run B: groups 5–7 (length 3).
frames.zh: 找出连续零组：A 两组，B 三组

frames.t: Rule 2: compress the longer run once
frames.zh: 把较长的 B 改成 ::

cards.t: Valid or invalid IP address? IP vs MAC
cards.tz: IP 地址是否有效？IP 与 MAC
cards.en:
Plain idea: check the format rules one by one.

  • IPv4: 4 decimal numbers, each 0-255 (8 bits), separated by dots. Hex is not used.
  • IPv6: 8 groups of up to 4 hex digits (0-9, a-f), separated by colons; "::" may appear once.
  • MAC: 6 pairs of hex digits (48 bits), e.g. 41:85:c4:ae:9d:01. Looks like IPv6 but has only 6 groups of 2.
AddressVerdict
19.29.0.256Invalid: 256 > 255
127.0.0.1Valid IPv4
0.0.0.0Valid IPv4 (lowest)
aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ffNot IP; a MAC address format (6 × 8 bits)
2001:0db8:85h3:...Invalid: 'h' is not hex
2001:db8::ff00:42:8329Valid IPv6 (shortened)

IP vs MAC: IP addresses are changeable, assigned (via the ISP, under ICANN) and used to find a device's location in a network; routers use them. MAC addresses are fixed by the manufacturer and identify the device on the local network; switches use them, and they are also used for MAC address filtering. On Windows, ipconfig shows a device's IP address.

Exam wording: Each number in an IPv4 address is 8 bits, so it must be from 0 to 255.
cards.zh:
简单理解：逐条检查格式规则。

  • IPv4：4 个十进制数，每个 0-255（8 bits），以点分隔，不用十六进制。
  • IPv6：8 组、每组最多 4 个十六进制数字（0-9、a-f），以冒号分隔；「::」只可出现一次。
  • MAC：6 对十六进制（48 bits），如 41:85:c4:ae:9d:01，似 IPv6 但只有 6 组、每组 2 位。
地址判断
19.29.0.256无效：256 > 255
127.0.0.1有效 IPv4
0.0.0.0有效 IPv4（最小）
aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff不是 IP；是 MAC 地址格式
2001:0db8:85h3:...无效：h 不是十六进制
2001:db8::ff00:42:8329有效 IPv6（简写）

IP 与 MAC：IP 地址可改变，经 ISP 分配（由 ICANN 管理），用来找出设备在网络中的位置，router 使用。MAC 地址由厂商固定，用来识别本地网络上的设备，switch 使用，亦用于 MAC address filtering。Windows 用 ipconfig 查看 IP 地址。

考试写法：Each number in an IPv4 address is 8 bits, so it must be from 0 to 255.

ex.q: Is 192.168.300.1 a valid IP address?
ex.a:
1. It has 4 parts, so it looks like IPv4.
2. 300 > 255, but each part is only 8 bits (max 255).
3. So it is invalid.

ex.q: Classify: fd00:61f6::612b:0:80ce and 41:85:c4:ae:9d:01.
ex.a:
1. fd00:61f6::612b:0:80ce: IPv6 (hex groups, one '::').
2. 41:85:c4:ae:9d:01: MAC address (6 pairs of hex = 48 bits).
ex.az:
1. 前者 IPv6。
2. 后者 MAC 地址。

ex.q: A student says: "IPv4 addresses can be written in hexadecimal like IPv6, so 'A0.1.2.3' is valid." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: IPv4 is written in decimal dot notation.
2. 'A0' is not a decimal number, so the address is invalid (it should be 160.1.2.3).
ex.az:
1. 错误：IPv4 用十进制点分记法。
2. 'A0' 无效，应写 160.1.2.3。

cards.en:
Analogy: you save a friend as "Mum" in your phone instead of remembering 9123 4567. A domain name is the easy name; the IP address is the number.

  • Domain name = a human-readable, meaningful form of an IP address; must be unique on the Internet.
  • FQDN (Fully Qualified Domain Name) = the full name with all levels, separated by dots.
wwwgooglecom.
hostnameregistration nametop-level domainroot (usually omitted)
  • You register the registration name + TLD (e.g. google.com).
  • The hostname (www, mail, ftp) is chosen freely by the owner – no extra registration.

Exam wording: A domain name is a human-readable and meaningful form of an IP address. An FQDN consists of all domain levels in the DNS hierarchy, each delimited by a period.
cards.zh:
比喻：手机里存“妈妈”而不是记 9123 4567。Domain name 是易记名字，IP 是号码。

  • Domain name：IP address 的易读、有意义形式，须在互联网上唯一。
  • FQDN：包含所有层级的完整名称，以句点分隔。
wwwgooglecom.
hostnameregistration nameTLDroot（通常省略）
  • 要注册的是 registration name + TLD。
  • Hostname（www、mail）由拥有者自定，不用另注册。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Identify hostname, registration name and TLD of mail.abccollege.edu.hk.
ex.a:
1. Hostname: mail.
2. Registration name: abccollege.
3. TLD: edu.hk (type 'edu' + country 'hk').
Domain name = abccollege.edu.hk; FQDN = mail.abccollege.edu.hk.
ex.az: hostname mail；registration name abccollege；TLD edu.hk。

ex.q: Is www.shop.hk the same FQDN as shop.hk?
ex.a:
1. No. www.shop.hk includes the hostname www.
2. shop.hk is the domain name only.
3. They may point to different IP addresses.
ex.az: 不同；前者多了 hostname，可指向不同 IP。

ex.q: Student: "In www.abc.com, www is the top-level domain." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The TLD is the right-most part: com.
2. www is the hostname (left-most).
ex.az: TLD 是最右边的 com；www 是 hostname。

cards.en:
Idea: the right-most part of a domain name tells you what kind of organisation, or where.

  • gTLD (generic TLD) – by type of organisation: com (commercial), edu (education), gov (government), org (non-profit), net (network provider).
  • ccTLD (country code TLD) – by country/region: hk, cn, jp, uk, au.
  • Combined: .com.hk, .gov.hk, .edu.hk.

Who manages it? ICANN accredits TLD registration; ICANN-accredited registrars (e.g. GoDaddy, HKDNR) sell/manage names. You search and register through a domain name registrar. Each different TLD is a separate domain to register.

Exam wording: gTLD indicates the type of organisation; ccTLD indicates the country or region. Domain names are registered through ICANN-accredited registrars.
cards.zh:
概念：域名最右部分说明机构类型或地区。

  • gTLD：按机构类型：com、edu、gov、org、net。
  • ccTLD：按国家/地区：hk、cn、jp、uk。
  • 可合并：.com.hk、.gov.hk、.edu.hk。

管理：ICANN 认可 TLD 注册，由 ICANN-accredited registrars（GoDaddy、HKDNR）管理分配；公众经 domain name registrar 注册。不同 TLD 要分别注册。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Alan wants www.star.edu.hk, www.star.hk and www.star.com. How many domains must he register? Does mail.star.com need registering?
ex.a:
1. star.edu.hk, star.hk, star.com have different TLDs → 3 registrations.
2. mail.star.com: 'mail' is just a hostname under star.com → no extra registration.
ex.az: 要注册 3 个；mail 只是 hostname。

ex.q: Classify the TLD of: (a) www.gov.hk (b) www.redcross.org (c) www.bbc.co.uk
ex.a:
(a) gov + hk: gTLD-type with ccTLD (Hong Kong government).
(b) org: gTLD (non-profit).
(c) uk: ccTLD (co = commercial within UK).
ex.az: (a) gov.hk (b) org gTLD (c) uk ccTLD。

ex.q: Student: ".hk is a gTLD because many companies use it." Correct it.
ex.a: .hk is a ccTLD: it shows the region (Hong Kong), not the type of organisation.
ex.az: .hk 是 ccTLD，表示地区。

cards.t: How many domain names to register? Second-level domains
cards.tz: 要注册多少个域名？二级域名
cards.en:
Plain idea: you register the part above the hostname (registration name + TLD). Hostnames like www, web, mail are free to add yourself.

FQDN www.google.com. = hostname www + registration name google + TLD com + root domain . (the final dot, usually omitted). Read the levels from the right: TLD is the top level; the next one to the left is the second-level domain.

Worked example (book type): a school wants web.getfivestarstar.edu.hk, www.getfivestarstar.hk, www.getfivestarstar.com, web.getfivestarstar.com, www.getfivestarstar.edu.hk.

  1. Remove the hostnames (www, web).
  2. Distinct domain names left: getfivestarstar.edu.hk, getfivestarstar.hk, getfivestarstar.com.
  3. Answer: 3. Adding mail.getfivestarstar.com later needs no new registration.

Choosing a domain: an education centre in Hong Kong fits .edu.hk; .gov.hk is for government; .org for general organisations, so an online shop on .org.hk is not appropriate.

Why not just use an IP address? IP addresses are hard to remember and may change; a domain name is meaningful and builds the brand.

Exam wording: Only the registration name with its top-level domain needs to be registered; hostnames can be created by the owner.
cards.zh:
简单理解：要注册的是主机名以上的部分（注册名 + TLD）。www、web、mail 等主机名可自行加入。

FQDN www.google.com. = 主机名 www + 注册名 google + TLD com + 根域 .（最后的点，通常省略）。由右向左读：TLD 是最高层，其左边一层是二级域名（second-level domain）。

例题（课本题型）：学校想用 web.getfivestarstar.edu.hk、www.getfivestarstar.hk、www.getfivestarstar.com、web.getfivestarstar.com、www.getfivestarstar.edu.hk。

  1. 去掉主机名（www、web）。
  2. 剩下不同的域名：getfivestarstar.edu.hk、getfivestarstar.hk、getfivestarstar.com。
  3. 答案：3 个。之后加 mail.getfivestarstar.com 不用再注册。

选域名：香港教育中心适合 .edu.hk；.gov.hk 属政府；.org 属一般机构，网店用 .org.hk 不恰当。

为何不直接用 IP？IP 难记又可能改变；域名有意义、利于品牌。

考试写法：Only the registration name with its top-level domain needs to be registered; hostnames can be created by the owner.

ex.q: In http://www.abc123.edu.hk/all/files.html, what is the second-level domain?
ex.a:
1. Read from the right: hk (TLD), then edu.
2. So the second-level domain is edu.
ex.az:
1. 由右读：hk 后是 edu。
2. 二级域名是 edu。

ex.q: A shop wants www.starshop.com, shop.starshop.com and www.starshop.com.hk. How many domain names to register?
ex.a:
1. Remove hostnames: starshop.com, starshop.com, starshop.com.hk.
2. Distinct: starshop.com and starshop.com.hk.
3. Answer: 2.
ex.az:
1. 去掉主机名。
2. 不同的有 starshop.com、starshop.com.hk。
3. 2 个。

ex.q: A student counts www.example.com and mail.example.com as 2 registrations. Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: www and mail are only hostnames.
2. Both are under the same registered domain example.com, so only 1 registration.
ex.az:
1. 错误：www、mail 只是主机名。
2. 只需注册 example.com 一个。

cards.tz: DNS 伺服器与名称解析
cards.en:
Analogy: your phone's contacts turn "Mum" into a phone number. A DNS server turns a domain name into an IP address. You could also just dial the number = type the IP in the browser.

  • DNS (Domain Name System) server: translates domain names → IP addresses. This is name resolution.
  • Usually provided by the ISP; public ones exist, e.g. 8.8.8.8.
  • If it doesn't know the answer, it asks other DNS servers (root → TLD → the domain's own server) and remembers (caches) the result.
  • nslookup www.example.hk shows the IP(s). One name may map to several IPs.
  • DNS uses port 53.

Typical fault: site opens by IP but not by name → DNS problem.

Also note: the DNS server's location is given as an IP address (usually from the ISP; public ones such as 8.8.8.8). nslookup + an FQDN shows a site's IP address. One domain name may have several IP addresses (many servers). If the DNS server is down, you can still visit a site by typing its IP address. Name resolution is mainly for humans; IoT devices can talk by IP directly. Blocking by domain name can be bypassed by typing the IP address.

Exam wording: A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses; this process is called name resolution.
cards.zh:
比喻：手机通讯录把“妈妈”变成电话号码；DNS server 把域名变成 IP。直接拨号 = 在浏览器输入 IP。

  • DNS server：把 domain name → IP address，这叫 name resolution。
  • 通常由 ISP 提供；亦有公共 DNS 8.8.8.8。
  • 不知道答案时会问 root → TLD → 该域名的伺服器，并缓存结果。
  • nslookup 可查 IP；一个名可对应多个 IP。DNS 用 port 53。

常见故障：输入 IP 能开、输入域名不能开 → DNS 出问题。

补充：DNS 服务器的位置以 IP 地址表示（通常由 ISP 提供；亦有公共 DNS 如 8.8.8.8）。nslookup + FQDN 可查网站 IP。一个域名可有多个 IP（多部服务器）。DNS 服务器失灵时，仍可直接输入 IP 地址浏览网站。域名解析主要是为人类而设；IoT 设备可直接用 IP 沟通。以域名封锁网站，可被直接输入 IP 绕过。

考试写法：A DNS server translates domain names into IP addresses; this process is called name resolution.

ex.q: Ben can open a site by its IP address but not by its URL. Most likely reason?
ex.a:
1. Typing the IP works, so connection, router and web server are fine.
2. The step that fails is name → IP.
3. So the DNS server is out of service/unreachable (or DNS setting wrong).
ex.az: 网络和 server 正常，问题在 name resolution：DNS server 故障。

ex.q: Describe what happens when you type www.example.hk for the first time.
ex.a:
1. PC asks its DNS server (ISP) for the IP.
2. DNS server doesn't know: asks root server → told to ask .hk TLD server.
3. TLD server → points to example.hk's authoritative server.
4. That server replies with the IP; DNS server caches it and returns it to the PC.
5. PC connects to the web server at that IP.
ex.az: PC 问 DNS → root → .hk → 权威伺服器，取得 IP 后连接 web server。

ex.q: Student: "The DNS server stores and sends the web page." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The DNS server only returns the IP address.
2. The web server at that IP sends the page (via HTTP/HTTPS).
ex.az: DNS 只回传 IP；网页由 web server 送出。

frames.en: PC: "What is the IP of www.example.hk?" → ISP's DNS server.
frames.zh: PC 问 ISP 的 DNS server

frames.en: DNS server doesn't have it cached; root says "ask the .hk server".
frames.zh: root 叫它问 .hk

frames.en: .hk server says "ask example.hk's authoritative server".
frames.zh: .hk 指向权威伺服器

frames.en: Authoritative server: "www.example.hk = 203.0.113.80". DNS server caches it.
frames.zh: 取得 IP 并缓存

frames.en: DNS server returns the IP to the PC; the PC now sends its HTTP request to 203.0.113.80.
frames.zh: PC 用 IP 连接 web server

cards.en:
Analogy: a URL is a full delivery instruction: how to deliver (protocol), which building (host), which office (port), which shelf (path).

http://www.example.hk:80/about/network.html

PartExampleMeaning
1 Protocolhttprules both client and server follow
2 FQDN / IPwww.example.hkidentifies the host
3 Port80identifies the application on the host
4 Path/about/network.htmllocation of the resource from the root

Exam wording: A URL (Uniform Resource Locator) identifies the specific location of a resource on the Internet. It consists of the network protocol, the FQDN/IP address, the port number and the path.
cards.zh:
比喻：URL 是完整送货指示：怎样送（protocol）、哪座大厦（host）、哪个办公室（port）、哪个架（path）。

http://www.example.hk:80/about/network.html

部分例意思
Protocolhttp双方遵守的规则
FQDN/IPwww.example.hk识别主机
Port80识别主机上的应用
Path/about/network.html资源相对 root 的位置

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Split https://192.168.0.10:8443/admin/login.html.
ex.a:
1. Protocol: https.
2. Host: 192.168.0.10 (an IP instead of FQDN).
3. Port: 8443.
4. Path: /admin/login.html.
ex.az: https / 192.168.0.10 / 8443 / /admin/login.html。

ex.q: Split ftp://files.ict.hk/notes/ch2.pdf. What port is used?
ex.a:
1. Protocol ftp; host files.ict.hk; path /notes/ch2.pdf.
2. No port written → FTP default (21).
ex.az: ftp、files.ict.hk、/notes/ch2.pdf；预设 port 21。

ex.q: Student: "In http://www.example.hk/about, 'about' is the port." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. The port comes after a colon (:80).
2. /about is the path (folder).
ex.az: Port 写在冒号后；/about 是 path。

cards.en:
Analogy: the IP address is a hotel's phone number; the port is the room extension. One server can run a web server, a mail server, a DNS server… the port says which one.

  • Port number identifies a specific application/service on a host.
  • Servers listen on a port for requests.
  • If a URL has no port, the browser uses the default.
ServicePort
HTTP80
HTTPS443
DNS53
FTP21
SMTP25

Also note: other well-known (reserved) ports: 53 = DNS, 443 = HTTPS, 80 = HTTP. Analogy: the IP address is the hotel's phone number; the port is the room extension.

Exam wording: More than one application may run on the same host, so a port number is used to identify a specific application. Default ports: HTTP 80, HTTPS 443.
cards.zh:
比喻：IP 是酒店总机，port 是房间分机。同一台 server 可同时跑网页、邮件、DNS，port 说明找哪一个。

  • Port number 识别主机上的特定应用/服务。
  • Server 在某 port 监听请求。
  • URL 没写 port 就用预设。
服务Port
HTTP80
HTTPS443
DNS53
FTP21
SMTP25

补充：其他常见保留端口：53 = DNS、443 = HTTPS、80 = HTTP。比喻：IP 地址是酒店电话，端口是房间分机。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Which port is used by https://www.bank.hk/login and http://www.bank.hk:8080/?
ex.a:
1. First: no port → HTTPS default 443.
2. Second: written explicitly → 8080.
ex.az: 第一个 443；第二个 8080。

ex.q: Is http://www.abc.hk:80/ the same as http://www.abc.hk/? Explain.
ex.a: Yes. HTTP's default port is 80, so leaving it out gives the same port.
ex.az: 相同；HTTP 预设就是 80。

ex.q: Student: "Port 443 is used by HTTP because it is more secure." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. 443 is HTTPS's default; HTTP is 80.
2. A port number itself gives no security; HTTPS is secure because of SSL/TLS encryption.
ex.az: 443 是 HTTPS；HTTP 是 80。安全来自加密，不是 port。

cards.en:
Analogy: the path is like a folder path in File Explorer: start at the root, open folders, then the file.

  • Path = location of the resource relative to the web server's root.
  • In /about/network.html: about = folder, network.html = file.
  • No file name? The server sends index.html by default.
  • A URL is invalid if the folder/file does not exist exactly there (wrong folder, wrong extension, wrong name).

Exam wording: A path is the specific location of a resource relative to the root. If no file name is specified, index.html is loaded by default.
cards.zh:
比喻：Path 像 File Explorer 的路径：由 root 开始，进资料夹，再到文件。

  • Path：资源相对 web server root 的位置。
  • /about/network.html：about 是 folder，network.html 是文件。
  • 没写文件名就预设载入 index.html。
  • 如该位置没有该 folder/file（放错资料夹、扩展名错），URL 无效。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Root has index.html and folder news/ containing 2026.html. Valid? (1) http://a.hk/ (2) http://a.hk/news/2026.html (3) http://a.hk/2026.html
ex.a:
(1) valid: loads index.html.
(2) valid.
(3) invalid: 2026.html is in news/, not root.
ex.az: (3) 无效，文件在 news 里。

ex.q: Root has folder img/ with logo.png. Is http://a.hk/img/logo.jpg valid?
ex.a: No. The file is logo.png; the extension must match exactly.
ex.az: 无效，扩展名不同。

ex.q: Student: "http://a.hk/news/ is invalid because no file is named." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. With no file name, the server looks for index.html in news/.
2. It is valid if news/index.html exists.
ex.az: 没写文件名会找 news/index.html，存在就有效。

cards.t: Folder paths and checking if a URL is valid
cards.tz: 文件夹路径与判断 URL 是否有效
cards.en:
Plain idea: a URL path works like a file path on your PC. Each "/" goes one folder deeper from the root.

On a PC: C:\Users\Guest\Desktop\example.pdf: C:\ is the root; Desktop is the current directory (a subdirectory of Guest); .pdf is the file extension.

Worked example: site www.ict.org.hk has: / contains index.html, questionbank.html, folders en (q1.png, q2.png), hk (q1.png, q2.png) and soln, which contains q1.png, q2.png.

URLValid?
/en/q1.pngYes: q1.png is in en
/soln/q1.pngYes
/hk/index.htmlNo: index.html is in the root, not in hk
/index.htmlYes

If a URL ends at a folder (no file name), the browser looks for index.html by default.

Exam wording: The path refers to the location of the resource relative to the root directory of the host.
cards.zh:
简单理解：URL 路径与电脑文件路径一样，每个「/」由根目录向下走一层文件夹。

电脑中：C:\Users\Guest\Desktop\example.pdf：C:\ 是根目录；Desktop 是目前目录（Guest 的子目录）；.pdf 是扩展名。

例题：www.ict.org.hk 的根目录有 index.html、questionbank.html，以及文件夹 en（q1.png、q2.png）、hk（q1.png、q2.png）、soln（q1.png、q2.png）。

URL有效？
/en/q1.png有效
/soln/q1.png有效
/hk/index.html无效：index.html 在根目录，不在 hk
/index.html有效

URL 只到文件夹（无文件名）时，浏览器默认找 index.html。

考试写法：The path refers to the location of the resource relative to the root directory of the host.

ex.q: In http://www.example.hk:80/about/network.html, what do /about and /network.html mean?
ex.a:
1. /about: a folder called about under the root.
2. /network.html: a file inside the about folder.
ex.az:
1. /about 是根目录下的文件夹。
2. network.html 是其中的文件。

ex.q: Using the ict.org.hk structure, is http://www.ict.org.hk/soln/hk/q1.png valid?
ex.a:
1. soln contains only q1.png and q2.png.
2. There is no hk folder inside soln.
3. So it is invalid.
ex.az:
1. soln 内只有两个 png。
2. 没有 soln/hk。
3. 无效。

ex.q: A student says http://www.ict.org.hk/en/ shows an error because no file name is given. Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: with no file name, the browser asks for the default file index.html in that folder.
2. It only fails if that folder has no index.html.
ex.az:
1. 错误：没文件名会找该文件夹的 index.html。
2. 只有该文件夹没有 index.html 才出错。

cards.en:
Idea: exams mix many kinds of addresses. Look at the shape.

TypeShapeExample
IPv44 decimals 0–255, dots10.0.0.1
IPv6hex groups, colons, maybe ::fe80::1
MAC6 pairs of hex (48 bits)00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E
Domain nameregistration name + TLDgoogle.com
FQDNhostname + domain namewww.google.com
URLprotocol:// + host + pathhttps://www.google.com/maps

Tip: MAC has exactly 6 groups of 2 hex digits; IPv6 has up to 8 groups of up to 4.

Exam wording: name the type and give the reason by its format, e.g. "IPv6, because it uses hexadecimal groups separated by colons."
cards.zh:
概念：按外形辨认。

类型外形例
IPv44 个 0–255 十进制，句点10.0.0.1
IPv6十六进制组，冒号，可有 ::fe80::1
MAC6 对十六进制 (48 bits)00:1A:2B:3C:4D:5E
Domain nameregistration name + TLDgoogle.com
FQDNhostname + domainwww.google.com
URLprotocol:// + host + pathhttps://www.google.com/maps

考试写法：写出类型并用格式说明理由。

ex.q: Classify: (a) 2001:db8::7 (b) ftp://files.ict.hk/a.zip (c) AC:DE:48:00:11:22 (d) www.rthk.hk
ex.a:
(a) IPv6 – hex, colons, ::.
(b) URL – has protocol and path.
(c) MAC – 6 pairs of hex.
(d) FQDN – hostname www + domain.
ex.az: (a) IPv6 (b) URL (c) MAC (d) FQDN。

ex.a: It looks like IPv4 but 300 > 255, so it is not a valid IPv4 address.
ex.az: 300 超过 255，不是有效 IPv4。

ex.q: Student calls AC:DE:48:00:11:22 an IPv6 address. Why wrong?
ex.a:
1. It has exactly 6 groups of 2 hex digits = 48 bits → MAC address.
2. IPv6 is 128 bits: 8 groups of up to 4 hex digits.
ex.az: 6 组 2 位 hex = MAC；IPv6 是 8 组 4 位。

cards.en:
Analogy: HTTP is sending a postcard: anyone handling it can read it. HTTPS is a locked box: only the receiver can open it.

  • HTTP (HyperText Transfer Protocol): used by the Web to transfer web pages (hypertext). The browser is the HTTP client; the web server answers.
  • HTTPS: HTTP + SSL/TLS encryption. Data is encrypted during transmission, so interceptors see scrambled text. Used for banking, shopping, logins. Browser shows a lock; the site has an SSL certificate proving its identity.
HTTPHTTPS
URL startshttp://https://
Default port80443
EncryptionNoYes (SSL/TLS)
SecurityUnsecureSecure

Exam wording: HTTPS is a secure version of HTTP that uses SSL/TLS to encrypt data during transmission, ensuring confidentiality, so intercepted data cannot be read.
cards.zh:
比喻：HTTP 像明信片，经手的人都看得到；HTTPS 像上锁的箱子，只有收件人能开。

  • HTTP：WWW 用来传送网页（超文本）；浏览器是 HTTP client。
  • HTTPS：HTTP + SSL/TLS 加密，传输期间加密，截取者只看到乱码。用于网银、网购、登入；浏览器显示锁头，网站有 SSL certificate 证明身份。
HTTPHTTPS
开头http://https://
预设 port80443
加密否是

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Why should online banking use HTTPS?
ex.a:
1. With HTTP, password and account data travel as plain text; an interceptor can read them.
2. HTTPS encrypts them with SSL/TLS during transmission → unreadable if intercepted.
3. The certificate helps confirm it is the real bank.
ex.az: HTTP 明文可被读取；HTTPS 加密，并有证书确认身份。

ex.q: A shop's checkout page URL is http://shop.hk/pay. Give one risk and one fix.
ex.a:
Risk: card details are sent unencrypted and can be intercepted.
Fix: install an SSL certificate and serve the page over HTTPS (https://, port 443).
ex.az: 风险：资料未加密被截取；改用 HTTPS。

ex.q: Student: "HTTPS makes the website virus-free." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. HTTPS only encrypts data in transit and verifies the server.
2. It does not check the site's content for malware; a scam site can also have HTTPS.
ex.az: HTTPS 只加密传输，不保证网站无病毒。

cards.tz: HTTP 请求-回应与状态码
cards.en:
Analogy: a restaurant. You (browser) order (request); the kitchen (server) brings food or says "sold out" (response with a status).

  1. User types a URL; the FQDN is translated to an IP by DNS.
  2. Browser sends an HTTP request: GET = ask for a resource (a page); POST = send data to the server to process (a form).
  3. Server sends an HTTP response: a status code + the resource.
  4. Browser interprets the HTML and shows the page.
CodeMeaning
200OK
400Bad Request
403Forbidden (no permission)
404Not Found
500Internal Server Error
502 / 503 / 504Bad Gateway / Service Unavailable / Gateway Timeout

4xx = client-side problem, 5xx = server-side problem.

Exam wording: GET requests a resource from the server; POST submits data to the server for processing. 404 means the requested resource cannot be found on the server.
cards.zh:
比喻：餐厅：你（浏览器）点菜（request），厨房（server）上菜或说“卖完”（response + 状态码）。

  1. 输入 URL，DNS 把 FQDN 转成 IP。
  2. 浏览器发 HTTP request：GET 请求资源；POST 把数据交给 server 处理（表格）。
  3. Server 回 HTTP response：状态码 + 资源。
  4. 浏览器解读 HTML 并显示。

状态码：200 OK、400 Bad Request、403 Forbidden、404 Not Found、500 Internal Server Error、502/503/504。4xx 客户端问题，5xx 伺服器问题。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: A login form shows '404 Not Found'. Which method did it likely use; what does 404 mean?
ex.a:
1. A login form sends data for processing → POST.
2. 404: the server can't find the requested resource (e.g. wrong action path, page removed).
ex.az: 表格用 POST；404 找不到资源。

ex.q: Server is overloaded during course registration. Which code is most likely, and is it client or server side?
ex.a: 503 Service Unavailable – a 5xx code, so a server-side problem.
ex.az: 503，伺服器端问题。

ex.q: Student: "GET is used to upload a photo because it gets the photo from the user." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. GET requests a resource from the server.
2. Sending data (a photo, a form) to the server for processing uses POST.
ex.az: 上传/提交资料用 POST；GET 是向 server 索取资源。

frames.en: User types http://www.example.hk/
frames.zh: 输入 URL

frames.en: Browser asks DNS: www.example.hk → 203.0.113.80
frames.zh: DNS 解析成 IP

frames.en: GET /index.html HTTP/1.1 sent to 203.0.113.80 port 80
frames.zh: 发 GET request 到 port 80

frames.en: HTTP/1.1 200 OK + HTML of the page
frames.zh: 回 200 OK 和 HTML

frames.en: Browser interprets the HTML and shows the page to the user.
frames.zh: 浏览器显示网页

cards.en:
Analogy: SMTP is the postman delivering letters. POP3 is taking letters home from the post office box (the box is then empty). IMAP is keeping letters at the post office and reading them there from any branch.

  • Email system = user agents (email clients), email servers, email protocols.
  • SMTP: sends mail to the server, and from server to server.
  • POP3 / IMAP: clients retrieve mail from the server.
POP3IMAP
Where mail staysdownloaded to local device (deleted from server by default, can keep)kept on server
Many devicesnot syncedsynchronised
Offline readingyes after downloadneeds Internet

Webmail (e.g. Gmail in a browser) reaches the browser by HTTP/HTTPS.

Exam wording: SMTP is used to send emails to the email server. POP3 downloads emails to the local computer so they can be read offline; IMAP keeps emails on the server and synchronises them across multiple devices.
cards.zh:
比喻：SMTP 是邮差送信；POP3 是把信箱里的信拿回家（信箱就空了）；IMAP 是信留在邮局，哪间分局都可看。

  • 电邮系统 = user agents、email servers、email protocols。
  • SMTP：发送邮件到 server，及 server 之间传送。
  • POP3 / IMAP：从 server 收取。
POP3IMAP
邮件位置下载到本机（预设从 server 删除，可保留）留在 server
多设备不同步同步
离线阅读可以需上网

Webmail 经 HTTP/HTTPS 送到浏览器。

考试写法：同英文粗体句子。

ex.q: Match: (a) Outlook sends a message (b) phone, iPad and PC show same folders (c) read old mail on a plane on one laptop.
ex.a:
(a) SMTP.
(b) IMAP – mail stays on server and syncs.
(c) POP3 – mail was downloaded to the laptop.
ex.az: (a) SMTP (b) IMAP (c) POP3。

ex.q: List the protocols used when Alice (Outlook) emails Bob, who reads it in Apple Mail with IMAP.
ex.a:
1. Alice's client → her server: SMTP.
2. Her server → Bob's server: SMTP.
3. Bob's client ← his server: IMAP.
ex.az: SMTP → SMTP → IMAP。

ex.q: Student: "IMAP is used to send email." Correct it.
ex.a:
1. IMAP (and POP3) only retrieve mail from the server.
2. Sending uses SMTP.
ex.az: IMAP 是收取；发送用 SMTP。

demo.title: An email from Alice to Bob

frames.en: Alice clicks Send. Her client uploads the mail to her mail server using SMTP.
frames.zh: 客户端用 SMTP 送到自己的 server

frames.en: Alice's server looks up Bob's mail server (via DNS) and passes the mail on with SMTP.
frames.zh: server 之间用 SMTP

frames.en: POP3: Bob's client downloads the mail to his laptop; by default it is removed from the server. Readable offline.
frames.zh: POP3：下载到本机，可离线读

cards.t: Email protocol misconceptions: POP3 deletion and webmail
cards.tz: 电邮协定误解：POP3 删除与网页电邮
cards.en:
Trap 1: "After POP3 downloads emails, the server always deletes them." Wrong. By default they are deleted to free space, but POP3 clients have the option to keep emails on the server.

Trap 2: "Webmail (e.g. Gmail in a browser) uses IMAP/POP3 to receive mail." Wrong. In web-based email, mail goes from the mail server to the browser using HTTP/HTTPS. A mail server offering only webmail needs HTTP/HTTPS for users, while SMTP is still used to send between servers.

Choosing POP3 or IMAP:

  • Small mailbox (e.g. 1 GB or 2 MB) → POP3: emails are downloaded to the local computer, freeing server space.
  • Many devices / access from any computer → IMAP: emails stay on the server and are synchronised.

Webmail pros: no client software to install; access from any computer with a browser. Cons: needs Internet to read; mail stored on provider's server (privacy, storage limits).

Exam wording: Web-based email is delivered from the mail server to the browser using HTTP/HTTPS, not POP3/IMAP.
cards.zh:
陷阱 1：「POP3 下载后服务器一定删除电邮」——错。预设会删除以腾出空间，但 POP3 客户端可选择把电邮保留在服务器。

陷阱 2：「网页电邮（如浏览器中的 Gmail）用 IMAP/POP3 收信」——错。网页电邮由邮件服务器经 HTTP/HTTPS 传到浏览器。只提供网页电邮的服务器，对用户只需 HTTP/HTTPS；服务器之间传送仍用 SMTP。

选 POP3 还是 IMAP：

  • 邮箱小（如 1 GB、2 MB）→ POP3：下载到本机，腾出服务器空间。
  • 多部设备／任何电脑都要存取 → IMAP：电邮留在服务器并同步。

网页电邮优点：不用装软件；任何有浏览器的电脑都可用。缺点：要上网才能读；电邮存于供应商服务器（私隐、容量限制）。

考试写法：Web-based email is delivered from the mail server to the browser using HTTP/HTTPS, not POP3/IMAP.

ex.a:

1. POP3。
2. 下载到本机，服务器空间不易满。

ex.az:

cards.t: FTP and application protocols on TCP/IP
cards.tz: FTP 与 TCP/IP 上的应用协定
cards.en:
Idea: TCP/IP is the delivery system; application protocols decide what the messages mean.

  • FTP (File Transfer Protocol): transfers files between a client and a file server. User authentication (username + password) is usually required. Clients: WinSCP, FileZilla. Common use: uploading website files to a web host.
  • HTTP, HTTPS, SMTP, POP3, IMAP, FTP, DNS are application protocols that run on top of TCP/IP.
NeedProtocol
view web pageHTTP/HTTPS
send emailSMTP
receive emailPOP3 / IMAP
upload/download filesFTP
name → IPDNS

Exam wording: FTP is used to transfer files between a client and a file server over a network; user authentication is usually required. HTTP, SMTP, POP3, IMAP and FTP are application protocols on top of TCP/IP.
cards.zh:
概念：TCP/IP 是运输系统；应用协定决定讯息代表什么。

  • FTP：在 client 与 file server 之间传送文件，通常需要用户认证（帐户+密码）。工具：WinSCP、FileZilla。常用来把网站文件上载到主机。
  • HTTP、HTTPS、SMTP、POP3、IMAP、FTP、DNS 都是建立在 TCP/IP 之上的应用协定。

cards.en:
Analogy: imagine every object at home could "talk": the fridge tells your phone the milk is finished, the aircon hears you are coming home. That talking network of things is the Internet of Things (IoT).

How it works

  • Sensor = a part that measures something (temperature, location, motion).
  • The object sends the data through a wireless technology: Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, RFID (Radio Frequency Identification, a tag read by radio) or NFC (Near Field Communication, very short range, e.g. tapping a card).
  • IoT makes a huge amount of data every second, so it is stored and processed by cloud computing.
  • Based on the result, objects take actions automatically.

Examples: smart speakers, smart homes (lights/aircon controlled remotely), smart bands, cars sending speed and location for real-time arrival time.

Exam wording: IoT refers to a network connecting different objects. The connected objects share collected data and provide new functionalities. IoT collects the data; cloud computing stores and processes it in real time; objects then act automatically.
cards.zh:
比喻：如果家里每样东西都会“说话”：雪柜告诉手机牛奶没了，冷气知道你快到家。这个会说话的物件网络就是 Internet of Things (IoT，物联网)。

运作

  • Sensor（感应器）= 量度东西的部件（温度、位置、动作）。
  • 物件用无线技术传数据：Wi-Fi、Bluetooth、RFID（无线射频识别标签）、NFC（近场通讯，极短距离，例如拍卡）。
  • IoT 每秒产生大量数据，要靠 cloud computing 储存及处理。
  • 按处理结果，物件自动采取行动。

例子：智能喇叭、智能家居、智能手环、车辆传速度和位置计算预计到达时间。

考试写法：IoT refers to a network connecting different objects. The connected objects share collected data and provide new functionalities. IoT 收集数据，cloud 储存及实时分析，物件再自动行动。

ex.q: A smart aircon turns on when the owner's phone is within 1 km of home. Identify the IoT elements.
ex.a:
1. Connected objects: phone and aircon.
2. Data collected: the phone's GPS location.
3. Network: location sent by mobile data / Wi-Fi to a cloud server.
4. Processing: cloud checks if distance < 1 km.
5. Action: server sends a command, aircon switches on automatically.
ex.az:
1. 物件：手机和冷气。
2. 数据：手机 GPS 位置。
3. 经流动数据／Wi-Fi 送到云端。
4. 云端判断距离是否少于 1 km。
5. 发指令，冷气自动开。

ex.q: Explain why IoT relies on cloud computing.
ex.a:
1. IoT devices produce a huge amount of data every second.
2. The devices themselves have little storage and processing power.
3. Cloud servers can store and process the data through the Internet instantly.
4. So results come back in real time and devices can act automatically.
ex.az:
1. IoT 每秒产生大量数据。
2. 装置本身储存和运算能力小。
3. 云端可经 Internet 即时储存及处理。
4. 所以能实时回传结果，自动行动。

ex.q: A student writes: "A smart band is IoT because it has a screen." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Having a screen is not what makes it IoT.
2. It is IoT because it is connected: it collects data (heart rate, steps) and shares it over Bluetooth to a phone/cloud, giving new functions (health reports).
3. Right answer: mention collect data + share through a network + new functionality.
ex.az:
1. 有屏幕不是 IoT 的原因。
2. 它是 IoT 因为连网：收集心率步数，经 Bluetooth 分享到手机／云端，提供新功能。
3. 要写：收集数据 + 经网络分享 + 新功能。

frames.en: The phone's GPS sensor reads its location.

frames.zh: 数据经 Wi-Fi／流动网络传出。

frames.en: The cloud server stores the data and checks: distance < 1 km?
frames.zh: 云端储存数据并判断：距离 < 1 km？

frames.en: Cloud sends a command; the aircon switches on and the phone gets a notice.
frames.zh: 云端发指令，冷气自动开，手机收到通知。

cards.en:
Analogy: instead of keeping all your money under your bed, you put it in a bank and use it from any ATM. The cloud is the bank for your files and programs.

How it works: the cloud simply means the Internet. Data and programs are kept on remote servers hosted by a third party (the provider) and you reach them through the Internet. You don't need to upgrade your hardware or install lots of software.

BenefitMeaning
AccessibilityAccess data anywhere, anytime via the Internet
FlexibilityChange service plan on demand (e.g. buy more storage)
MaintenanceProvider handles maintenance, backup and upgrades

Limitations: needs an Internet connection; data kept by a third party (privacy/security concerns); ongoing subscription fees.

Exam wording: Everything in the cloud is stored in remote servers hosted by a third party and is accessible through the Internet.
cards.zh:
比喻：钱不放床底而放银行，在任何提款机都能用。Cloud 就是你文件和程式的“银行”。

运作：cloud 就是 Internet。数据和程式放在第三方托管的远端伺服器，经 Internet 使用，不用升级硬件或安装大量软件。

好处意思
Accessibility随时随地经 Internet 存取
Flexibility按需要改计划（如加空间）
Maintenance维护、备份、升级由供应商负责

限制：要连网；数据交第三方（私隐／保安）；持续月费。

考试写法：Everything in the cloud is stored in remote servers hosted by a third party and is accessible through the Internet.

ex.q: A school moves homework from a local file server to cloud storage. Give two benefits and one drawback.
ex.a:
1. Accessibility: students hand in/read homework anytime, anywhere.
2. Maintenance: the provider does backup and upgrades, saving the school's IT work.
3. Drawback: no Internet = no access; or data held by a third party raises privacy concerns.
ex.az:
1. 随时随地存取。
2. 维护备份由供应商负责。
3. 缺点：断网用不到／数据交第三方有私隐问题。

ex.q: A shop's online storage is full in December. Which cloud benefit helps?
ex.a:
1. Flexibility.
2. The shop can upgrade the plan on demand to get more storage at once.
3. No need to buy and install new hard disks.
ex.az:
1. Flexibility。
2. 可即时加购空间。
3. 不用买新硬碟。

ex.q: A student says: "Cloud data is safe because it is not on my computer." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: being off your computer does not make data safe.
2. The data sits on a third party's servers and travels over the Internet, so there are privacy and security concerns (leaks, hacking).
3. Correct view: cloud gives backup by the provider, but you still need strong passwords / 2FA.
ex.az:
1. 错：不在自己电脑不等于安全。
2. 数据在第三方伺服器并经 Internet 传送，有私隐及保安风险。
3. 正确：供应商有备份，但仍要强密码／2FA。

frames.en: You use a laptop and a phone.
frames.zh: 你用手提电脑和手机。

frames.en: Both connect through the Internet.
frames.zh: 两者经 Internet 连接。

frames.en: Files live on the provider's servers, so any device sees the same latest copy.
frames.zh: 文件在供应商伺服器，任何装置看到同一最新版本。

cards.en:
Analogy: renting from a cloud is like renting at a hotel: you can rent the whole room (a computer), just a locker (storage), or use the gym (a ready app).

TypeWhat you rentExamples
Operating system (virtual machines)Run tasks on more powerful virtual machines (a computer simulated by software on the server)Microsoft Azure, Google Compute Engine
StorageStore data on remote servers hosted by a third partyGoogle Drive, OneDrive, iCloud
Hosted applicationOpen and use software from the cloud server without installing itGoogle Docs Editors, Office 365

Cloud also powers collaboration tools: users share and co-edit files in real time.

Exam wording: name the type, then say what is on the server: "the program runs on the cloud server, so no installation is needed on the local computer".
cards.zh:
比喻：像住酒店：可以租整间房（一部电脑）、只租储物柜（储存）、或用现成健身室（应用程式）。

类型租什么例子
Operating system (virtual machines)在云端更强的虚拟机（软件模拟的电脑）运行工作Azure、Google Compute Engine
Storage数据放第三方伺服器Google Drive、OneDrive、iCloud
Hosted application在云端直接用软件，不用安装Google Docs、Office 365

云端亦支援协作工具：多人实时共同编辑。

考试写法：写出类型，再写 the program runs on the cloud server, so no installation is needed。

ex.q: Classify: (i) renting a powerful server to train a model; (ii) backing up photos to iCloud; (iii) writing an essay in Google Docs.
ex.a:
1. (i) needs computing power → virtual machine / OS service.
2. (ii) only keeps files → storage.
3. (iii) software used in browser without install → hosted application.
ex.az:
1. 要运算力 → 虚拟机。
2. 只存文件 → 储存。
3. 浏览器内用软件 → 托管应用。

ex.q: A low-spec Chromebook can still edit spreadsheets in Office 365. Why?
ex.a:
1. Office 365 is a hosted application.
2. The program runs on the cloud server; the Chromebook only shows the result in a browser.
3. So the local computer needs no installation and little power.
ex.az:
1. Office 365 是托管应用。
2. 程式在云端运行，本机只显示。
3. 所以本机不用安装、要求低。

ex.q: A student classifies Google Drive as a hosted application because "it is used in a browser". Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Using a browser is not the test.
2. Google Drive's main job is to keep files on remote servers → storage.
3. Google Docs (the editor) is the hosted application.
ex.az:
1. 用浏览器不是判断标准。
2. Drive 主要存文件 → storage。
3. Google Docs 编辑器才是 hosted application。

cards.en:
Analogy: a USB drive is like passing one notebook around the class; a cloud document is like a big whiteboard everyone can write on at the same time.

A group project could use (1) a USB drive passed around, (2) meeting after school while one person types, or (3) cloud-based document editing (e.g. Google Docs).

Cloud collaborationUSB / meeting
Edit simultaneously in real time, anywhereOne person edits at a time / must meet at same place and time
Only one up-to-date versionMany copies → version conflicts
Saved automatically, version history, commentsUSB can be lost or spread malware

Exam wording: "Members can edit the same document simultaneously in real time; there is only one up-to-date version, avoiding version inconsistency."
cards.zh:
比喻：USB 像全班轮流传一本簿；云端文件像一块大白板，大家可同时写。

小组项目方法：(1) USB 轮流传；(2) 放学见面一人打字；(3) 云端文件（Google Docs）。

云端协作USB／见面
多人同时实时编辑，随地可用一次一人／要同时同地
只有一个最新版本多个副本 → 版本混乱
自动储存、版本纪录、留言USB 会遗失或带病毒

考试写法：Members can edit the same document simultaneously in real time; there is only one up-to-date version, avoiding version inconsistency.

ex.q: Give two disadvantages of circulating a USB drive compared with cloud collaboration.
ex.a:
1. Only one member can edit at a time, so progress is slow.
2. Several copies exist, causing version inconsistency.
3. (Also accepted) the USB may be lost or spread malware.
ex.az:
1. 一次一人，慢。
2. 多个副本，版本不一致。
3. USB 可遗失／带病毒。

ex.q: A member deletes a paragraph by accident in a shared Google Doc. How can the group recover it?
ex.a:
1. Open the document's version history.
2. Find the version before the deletion.
3. Restore it (or copy the paragraph back).
ex.az:
1. 打开版本纪录。
2. 找删除前的版本。
3. 还原。

ex.q: A student says cloud collaboration works without Internet because the file is saved automatically. Correct it.
ex.a:
1. Wrong: real-time co-editing and auto-save to the server need an Internet connection.
2. Offline edits (if allowed) only sync when back online.
3. So a limitation of cloud collaboration is: requires Internet access.
ex.az:
1. 错：实时协作及自动存到伺服器要连网。
2. 离线修改要上线后才同步。
3. 限制：需要 Internet。

demo.title: Three ways to do a group project

frames.en: A → B → C: one person edits, then passes the drive. Copies multiply.
frames.zh: A→B→C 轮流，一次一人，副本越来越多。

frames.en: Everyone must be in the same place at the same time; one person types.
frames.zh: 要同时同地，一人打字。

frames.en: All members edit the single file on the server at the same time.
frames.zh: 所有人同时编辑伺服器上同一文件。

cards.en:
Analogy: a city that works like a body: sensors are the eyes, the network is the nerves, the cloud + AI is the brain, and traffic lights or street lights are the hands.

How it works: cloud-based IoT applications enabled smart cities. A smart city is a complex system of systems: connected systems use IoT data and take actions based on AI analysis. Goal: make better decisions and improve quality of life by addressing urbanisation challenges (environment, traffic congestion, waste management).

Hong Kong's Smart City Blueprint: Smart Economy, Smart Living, Smart Mobility, Smart Environment, Smart People, Smart Government.

Exam wording: sensors collect data → sent to cloud → analysed → automatic action in real time → name the area (e.g. Smart Mobility).
cards.zh:
比喻：城市像身体：感应器是眼睛，网络是神经，cloud + AI 是大脑，交通灯和街灯是手。

运作：云端 IoT 应用推动智慧城市。智慧城市是系统中的系统：互连系统用 IoT 数据，按 AI 分析行动，目的是改善决策和生活质素，应对城市化问题（环境、塞车、废物）。

香港六范畴：Smart Economy、Living、Mobility、Environment、People、Government。

考试写法：感应器收集 → 送云端 → 分析 → 实时自动行动 → 写出范畴。

ex.q: Explain how a smart traffic light system is a smart city application.
ex.a:
1. Detectors (IoT) count vehicles and pedestrians.
2. Data is sent to the cloud.
3. AI analysis adjusts green-light time in real time.
4. Congestion drops → Smart Mobility.
ex.az:
1. 侦测器数车和人。
2. 送云端。
3. AI 实时调整绿灯。
4. 减少塞车 → Smart Mobility。

ex.q: Which area does a bin fill-level sensor belong to, and how does it help?
ex.a:
1. Smart Environment.
2. Sensors report how full each bin is.
3. The system plans collection routes to only visit full bins → less fuel and time.
ex.az:
1. Smart Environment。
2. 感应器回报满载程度。
3. 只收满的桶，省油省时。

ex.q: A student says: "A smart city means every citizen has a smartphone." What is wrong?
ex.a:
1. Phones alone are not a smart city.
2. The key is connected systems using IoT data + AI analysis to act and solve urban problems.
3. Rewrite: "a system of systems that uses IoT data to make better decisions and improve quality of life".
ex.az:
1. 只有手机不算。
2. 关键是互连系统用 IoT 数据及 AI 行动解决城市问题。
3. 改写为“系统中的系统……改善生活质素”。

frames.en: Road sensors count cars and pedestrians at the junction.
frames.zh: 路口感应器数车和行人。

frames.en: Cloud AI compares flows from many junctions.
frames.zh: 云端 AI 比较多个路口的流量。

frames.en: Green time is lengthened for the busy direction, in real time.
frames.zh: 实时延长繁忙方向的绿灯。

cards.t: Smart Economy: online banking and payment
cards.tz: 智慧经济：网上银行与支付
cards.en:
Analogy: your money becomes a message: instead of handing over coins, your phone sends "pay $30 to this shop" to the bank.

  • Online banking: check up-to-date transactions (no waiting for the monthly statement), transfer money, pay bills 24/7.
  • Online payment platforms (PayPal, FPS = Faster Payment System, PPS): pay over the Internet; top up a digital wallet (stored-value account in an app) or link to a credit card / bank account. This boosted online shops and start-ups.
  • Contactless payment: Octopus card (NFC), credit/debit card (magnetic stripe, chip, NFC), mobile wallet (NFC, QR code).

Drawback: a shop that accepts only e-payment loses cash customers and may widen the digital divide (gap between people who can and cannot use IT).
