AV1 Video ExtensionVideoAV1Edge
Adobe AcrobatTextPDFMost
OSVideo playerAudio player
WindowsWindows Media PlayerGroove Music
macOSQuickTime PlayerMusic

Codec pack: a collection of audio/video codecs (e.g. K-Lite Codec Pack, free) that lets a player open many formats not supported by the OS or player.

Flash is gone: Adobe and major browsers ended Flash Player support at the end of 2020, so SWF and FLV are obsolete.

Exam wording: If the media player cannot play a file, update the player or install the missing codec (e.g. a codec pack).
cards.zh:
简单理解：浏览器播不到某格式就加插件；已下载的文件用媒体播放器；播放器仍失败就装 codec。

插件媒体格式浏览器
Web Media Extensions音讯OGGEdge
OpenH264影片MP4（H.264/AVC）Firefox
AV1 Video Extension影片AV1Edge
Adobe Acrobat文字PDF大部分
系统影片播放器音乐播放器
WindowsWindows Media PlayerGroove Music
macOSQuickTime PlayerMusic

Codec pack：一批音讯／影片 codec（如免费的 K-Lite Codec Pack），让播放器开启系统或播放器本身不支援的格式。

Flash 已终结：Adobe 及主要浏览器于 2020 年底停止支援 Flash Player，所以 SWF、FLV 已过时。

考试写法：If the media player cannot play a file, update the player or install the missing codec (e.g. a codec pack).

ex.q: Firefox cannot play an H.264 MP4 video. What can be installed?
ex.a:
1. The OpenH264 plug-in.
2. It lets Firefox decode MP4 (H.264/AVC) video.
ex.az:
1. OpenH264 插件。
2. 让 Firefox 解码 H.264。

ex.q: Ada downloaded a video, but QuickTime and Windows Media Player both fail even after updating. What next?
ex.a:
1. The needed codec is missing.
2. Install a codec pack such as K-Lite Codec Pack, then play again.
ex.az:
1. 缺少 codec。
2. 安装 K-Lite 等 codec pack。

ex.q: A student says: "Install the Flash plug-in to play old SWF games in Chrome." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: Flash Player support ended at the end of 2020.
2. Major browsers no longer run it, so SWF/FLV are obsolete.
ex.az:
1. 错误：Flash 已于 2020 年底停止支援。
2. SWF、FLV 已过时。

cards.en:
Analogy: downloading is filling a whole bucket before you drink. Streaming is drinking from a tap: water keeps flowing while you drink. A small cup under the tap (the buffer) keeps a little water ready in case the flow slows down.

Streaming is a technology used for delivering media over the Internet with a continuous flow of data. Users can play and download the media simultaneously, so waiting time is shortened.

On the client (user) side the player keeps a buffer = media data loaded in advance but not yet played:

played (removed)current position ▶buffer (loaded)not yet loaded
  • Playback starts once enough data is buffered; the player keeps downloading the rest from the streaming server.
  • If download rate < playback rate, the buffer empties and playback pauses (buffering).

Live stream = streaming a real-time event (sports, gaming, live shopping).

Exam wording: Streaming delivers media over the Internet as a continuous flow of data, so users can play and download the media simultaneously without waiting for the entire file.
cards.zh:
比喻：下载像先装满整桶水才喝；串流像直接对着水龙头喝，水一直流。水龙头下的小杯（buffer 缓冲）预先存一点水，以防水流变慢。

串流是以连续数据流经 Internet 传送媒体的技术，用户可一边下载一边播放，缩短等候时间。

用户端缓冲：已播放（移除）│播放位置│缓冲（已载入）│未载入。

  • 缓冲够就开始播放，同时继续从串流伺服器下载。
  • 下载速度 < 播放速度 → 缓冲用完 → 暂停（buffering）。

直播 live stream：实时串流活动。

Exam wording：Streaming delivers media as a continuous flow of data, so users can play and download simultaneously.

ex.q: A 4 Mbps video is streamed on a 3 Mbps connection with 10 s (40 Mb) already buffered. How long until it pauses?
ex.a:
1. Buffer drains at 4 − 3 = 1 Mb per second.
2. 40 Mb ÷ 1 Mb/s = 40 s.
3. After about 40 s playback pauses to buffer (unless the player lowers the quality).
ex.az: 每秒净减 1 Mb，40 Mb ÷ 1 = 40 秒后卡住。

ex.q: Explain why a streamed video can start within seconds while a downloaded one cannot.
ex.a:
1. Streaming only needs a small part (the buffer) before playing.
2. The rest is downloaded while you watch.
3. Downloading needs the whole file first.
ex.az: 串流只需先载入少量缓冲；下载要等整个文件。

ex.q: Lily says: 'With streaming, the whole video is saved on my phone after I watch it.' Correct her.
ex.a:
1. Wrong. Played data is removed from the buffer.
2. Streaming does not save the entire file, so it saves storage but cannot be replayed offline.
ex.az: 错。播完的数据会从缓冲移除，不会保存整个文件。

frames.en: Player asks the server for the video. Buffer = 0 s. Waiting…
frames.zh: 播放器向伺服器要影片，缓冲 0 秒。

frames.en: Data flows into the buffer. At 5 s buffered, playback starts.
frames.zh: 数据流入缓冲，够 5 秒就开始播放。

frames.en: Player takes data out of the buffer while the server keeps adding more. Played data is removed.
frames.zh: 一边播放一边下载，播完的数据移除。

frames.en: Download 3 Mbps < playback 4 Mbps → buffer shrinks every second.
frames.zh: 下载 3 < 播放 4，缓冲每秒减少。

frames.en: Buffer reaches 0 → spinning wheel (buffering) until enough data arrives again.
frames.zh: 缓冲用完 → 转圈等候。

cards.en:
Analogy: streaming is watching TV; downloading is buying the DVD.

StreamingDownloading
StartPlay in real time without downloading the entire fileWait for the whole file
StorageDoes not save the entire file → saves storage spaceUses local storage
OfflineNo offline playbackCan play offline
QualityBandwidth limits quality / smoothnessFull quality once downloaded
CopyrightHarder to copyEasy to copy

Streaming suits live events and on-demand video; downloading suits poor or no connections (e.g. flights).

Exam wording: Streaming allows playback in real time without downloading the entire file and saves storage space, but it cannot be played offline and the quality depends on the network bandwidth.
cards.zh:
比喻：串流像看电视；下载像买 DVD。

  • 串流：不用下载整个文件就能实时播放、省储存空间、较难复制；但不能离线、画质受带宽限制
  • 下载：要等完、占空间、易复制；但可离线、画质完整

直播及即点即播适合串流；网络差／无网络（如飞机上）适合下载。

Exam wording：Streaming: real-time playback without downloading the entire file, saves storage; no offline playback, quality depends on bandwidth.

ex.q: A school considers streaming lesson videos instead of letting students download them. Give one advantage and one disadvantage.
ex.a:
1. Advantage: videos play at once; no storage needed on students' devices; harder to copy.
2. Disadvantage: no offline playback, so students with poor connections suffer lag or low quality.
ex.az: 好处：即时播放、省空间。坏处：不能离线，网差会卡。

ex.q: Before a 12-hour flight, should Max stream or download his shows? Why?
ex.a:
1. Download.
2. There is no (or very expensive) Internet on the plane.
3. Downloaded files play offline at full quality.
ex.az: 下载：飞机上没网，下载后可离线播放。

ex.q: Ray says: 'Streaming uses less total data than downloading the same video at the same quality.' True?
ex.a:
1. Not true. To watch the whole video at the same quality, roughly the same amount of data must be transferred either way.
2. Streaming saves storage, not network data. Watching it twice by streaming even uses data twice.
ex.az: 错。同画质看完全片，传输量差不多；串流省的是储存空间，重看还要再耗数据。

demo.title: Same 60 s video: streaming vs downloading

frames.en: Streaming: starts filling a 5 s buffer. Downloading: starts fetching the whole file.
frames.zh: 串流：先填 5 秒缓冲；下载：开始下载全片。

frames.en: Streaming: buffer ready → playing. Downloading: 10% done, still waiting.
frames.zh: 串流已开始播放；下载只完成 10%。

frames.en: Downloading finishes → now it can play, and the file stays on the device (offline OK).
frames.zh: 下载完成才可播放，文件留在装置（可离线）。

frames.en: Streaming: nothing saved, storage free, needs network again to rewatch. Downloading: file uses storage, rewatch offline.
frames.zh: 串流不留文件；下载占空间但可离线重看。

cards.en:
Analogy: a full-course meal: dishes come one at a time and the table is cleared after each. You never wait for the whole meal to be cooked.

Buffer: media data already loaded ahead of the current playback position. Played data is removed after playing (saves storage). If there is enough buffer, playback is smooth even with brief congestion. When all the buffer is used up, the video pauses, drops frames or pixelates.

How to start streaming (creator side):

  1. Acquire video and audio sources in digital form.
  2. Encode them (after editing, or directly) into a suitable streaming format; check the platform's specifications.
  3. Protect & monetize: set viewing permission (e.g. block some regions) or charge.
  4. Distribute: upload to the streaming platform.
  5. Stream to viewers.

Exam wording: The client plays the media while it continues to download and buffer the remaining content; if the buffer runs out the playback pauses.
cards.zh:
比喻：全餐：一道一道上菜，吃完便收拾，不用等全部煮好。

缓冲（buffer）：在目前播放位置之前已载入的媒体数据。播放过的数据会被删除（省空间）。缓冲足够时，即使短暂网络挤塞也能流畅播放；缓冲用尽时就会停顿、跳格或出现马赛克。

开始串流（创作者）：

  1. Acquire 取得数码影音来源。
  2. Encode 编码（编辑后或直接）成合适串流格式；先看平台规格。
  3. Protect & monetize 保护及收费：设定观看权限（如封锁某些地区）或收费。
  4. Distribute 发布：上载到串流平台。
  5. Stream 串流给观众。

考试写法：The client plays the media while it continues to download and buffer the remaining content; if the buffer runs out the playback pauses.

ex.q: Why does a video keep pausing on a poor connection even though it started fine?
ex.a:
1. Playback uses data from the buffer.
2. A poor connection cannot refill the buffer fast enough.
3. When the buffer is used up, playback pauses.
ex.az:
1. 播放用缓冲数据。
2. 网络差，补充太慢。
3. 缓冲用尽就停顿。

ex.q: Put in order: Distribute, Acquire, Stream, Encode, Protect & monetize.
ex.a: 1. Acquire → 2. Encode → 3. Protect & monetize → 4. Distribute → 5. Stream.
ex.az: 1. 取得 → 2. 编码 → 3. 保护及收费 → 4. 发布 → 5. 串流。

ex.q: A student says: "Streaming saves the whole video on the phone, so it uses more storage." Correct this.
ex.a:
1. Mistake: streamed data is removed after playing.
2. Only a buffer is kept, so it saves storage compared with downloading the whole file.
ex.az:
1. 错误：播放后数据会删除。
2. 只保留缓冲，比下载整个文件省空间。

cards.t: Voice mail: voice calls and voice messages
cards.tz: 话音邮件：语音通话与语音讯息
cards.en:
Analogy: a voice call is talking face to face; a voice message is leaving a recorded note on someone's desk.

IM apps and social media offer both:

  • Voice calls enable real-time communication like phone calls, using VoIP (Voice over Internet Protocol) – voice turned into data packets and sent over the Internet. Some services can dial ordinary phone numbers.
  • Voice messaging allows users to deliver and receive messages anytime as an alternative to text messages. The audio is split and compressed into small files, so users hardly wait.
Voice callVoice message
Timingreal-time (synchronous)anytime (asynchronous)
Both online?yesno
Replayno (unless recorded)yes

Exam wording: Voice calls use VoIP to enable real-time communication like phone calls; voice messages can be delivered and received anytime as an alternative to text messages.
cards.zh:
比喻：语音通话像面对面说话；语音讯息像在对方桌上留一段录音。

  • 语音通话：像电话般实时沟通，用 VoIP（把声音变成数据封包经 Internet 传送）；部分服务可打普通电话号码。
  • 语音讯息：随时发送和接收，代替文字讯息；音频被分割压缩成小文件，几乎不用等。

通话：同步、双方要同时在线、不能重听；讯息：非同步、不用同时在线、可重听。

Exam wording：Voice calls use VoIP for real-time communication; voice messages can be delivered and received anytime.

ex.q: Why may a busy student prefer a voice message to a voice call with a teacher?
ex.a:
1. Voice messages are asynchronous: the teacher can listen and reply anytime.
2. They need not be online at the same time.
3. The message can be replayed.
ex.az: 不用同时在线、可随时听和回覆、可重播。

ex.q: Give one situation where a voice call is better than voice messages.
ex.a:
1. Discussing an urgent group-project problem that needs quick back-and-forth.
2. A call is real-time, so questions are answered instantly instead of waiting for replies.
ex.az: 紧急、需要即时来回讨论时，通话较好。

ex.q: Zoe thinks VoIP calls travel over the traditional telephone line, not the Internet. Correct her.
ex.a:
1. VoIP = Voice over Internet Protocol.
2. The voice is digitised, compressed and sent as data packets over the Internet (Wi-Fi or mobile data).
3. That's why IM calls use data, not phone minutes.
ex.az: VoIP 把声音变成数据封包经 Internet 传送，所以用的是数据而非电话线。

demo.title: A VoIP call, packet by packet

frames.en: Microphone records your voice.
frames.zh: 咪高峰录下声音。

frames.en: The app compresses the sound (audio codec) and splits it into small data packets.
frames.zh: 程式压缩声音并分成小封包。

frames.en: Packets travel over the Internet in real time.
frames.zh: 封包经 Internet 实时传送。

frames.en: Phone B decodes the packets and plays the voice within a fraction of a second. Both people talk at the same time → real-time.
frames.zh: B 解码播放，延迟极短，双方实时对话。

cards.en:
Analogy: video conferencing is a classroom discussion – everyone can speak. Webcasting is a school assembly broadcast – one stage, many listeners.

Video conferencing = real-time face-to-face meetings over the Internet, with screen sharing, chat and recording (e.g. Zoom, Teams). Webcasting is broadcasting live or pre-recorded audio or video over the Internet (Internet radio/TV, live-stream shopping).

Video conferencingWebcasting
Audiencehundreds or fewerunlimited / very large
Mediareal-timereal-time or pre-recorded
Communicationtwo-way, more interactionmainly one-way (live comments possible)
Privacyprivate eventspublic events

Exam wording: Video conferencing supports two-way real-time interaction for a relatively small group, suitable for private events; webcasting broadcasts live or pre-recorded media mainly one-way to a large audience, suitable for public events.
cards.zh:
比喻：视像会议像课堂讨论，人人可发言；网上广播像学校周会广播，一个台、很多听众。

视像会议：实时面对面网上会议，可分享画面、聊天、录影。Webcasting 网上广播：经 Internet 广播直播或预录影音。

  • 人数：会议数百或更少；广播无限／大量
  • 媒体：会议实时；广播实时或预录
  • 沟通：会议双向、多互动；广播主要单向（可开留言）
  • 私隐：会议适合私人活动；广播适合公开活动

Exam wording：Video conferencing: two-way, small group, private; webcasting: mainly one-way, large audience, public, live or pre-recorded.

ex.q: A school wants to show its Christmas talent show to all parents and the public. Video conferencing or webcasting?
ex.a:
1. Audience is large/unlimited.
2. Communication is mainly one-way.
3. It is a public event; can be live or pre-recorded.
Answer: webcasting.
ex.az: Webcasting：观众多、单向、公开。

ex.q: A teacher holds an online consultation with five students about their projects. Which and why?

2. Small group, needs two-way interaction (questions, screen sharing of their work).

ex.q: A company uses webcasting for a confidential board meeting 'because it supports more people'. Comment.

1. Wrong choice. Webcasting is for public, mainly one-way events.
2. A board meeting needs privacy and two-way discussion.
Right: video conferencing with access control (passcode/waiting room).
ex.az: 错。董事会要私隐和双向讨论，应用视像会议并设密码。

cards.en:
Plain idea: compare platforms on time limit, participant limit, cross-platform support and security.

Video conferencing lets people talk "face to face" with sound and video. Common extras: screen sharing, in-meeting chat, instant polling, group discussions. IM apps also do video calls, but usually for fewer people.

Worked example: a seminar has 70 students, 10 presenters and Q&A, about 1 hour.

Platform APlatform B

  2. Browser support: users can join without installing software.
  3. Meeting code + password: harder for outsiders to join without permission.
  4. End-to-end encryption: stops hackers stealing private information during transmission.

Exam wording: A unique meeting code and password prevent unauthorised people from entering; end-to-end encryption protects data during transmission.

cards.tz: 影响串流质素的技术因素
cards.en:
Analogy: streaming is pouring water through a pipe. Higher quality = more water per second. If the pipe (bandwidth) is too thin, it overflows → lag and blocky pictures.

The better the quality, the larger the file size. Sending large data with low bandwidth may cause latency (delay) and pixelisation (blocky picture). Factors:

  • Media format / codec – efficient compressed formats (MP4, AAC) recommended.
  • Bitrate – data per second; higher = better quality but needs more bandwidth.
  • Resolution – frame size (144p … 1080p, 4K); higher = sharper, more data.
  • Frame rate – frames per second (fps); higher = smoother motion, more data.
  • Network bandwidth of server and user, and connection stability – insufficient buffer causes pauses.

Streaming sites use adaptive streaming: automatically give the best quality the user's network can handle.

Data size = bitrate × time (bits ÷ 8 = bytes). E.g. 5 Mbps × 60 s = 300 Mb = 37.5 MB.

Exam wording: Higher bitrate, resolution and frame rate give better quality but need more bandwidth; if bandwidth is insufficient, latency and pixelisation occur. Adaptive streaming adjusts quality according to the user's network.
cards.zh:
比喻：串流像水经水管流过。画质高＝每秒水量大；水管（带宽）太幼就会塞 → 延迟和马赛克。

质素越好，文件越大。低带宽会出现延迟 latency 和画面马赛克 pixelisation。因素：

  • 格式／codec：用高效压缩格式（MP4、AAC）
  • Bitrate：每秒数据量，越高越清但要更多带宽
  • 解像度（144p…1080p、4K）
  • 帧率（fps）：越高越流畅，数据越多
  • 带宽及连线稳定性：缓冲不足会停顿

Adaptive streaming：按用户网速自动调整画质。

数据量 = bitrate × 时间（bit ÷ 8 = byte）。

Exam wording：Higher bitrate, resolution and frame rate need more bandwidth; insufficient bandwidth causes latency and pixelisation.

ex.q: Calculate the data used by streaming a 2-hour movie at 5 Mbps (1 MB = 8 Mb, 1 GB = 1000 MB).
Abby has a 2 GB monthly data plan. How many minutes of 1080p video at 8 Mbps can she stream?
Dan calculates 5 Mbps × 60 s = 300 MB. Find his mistake.
ex.a:
1. Mbps is megabits per second, not bytes.
2. 300 Mb ÷ 8 = 37.5 MB.
Always divide by 8 to convert bits to bytes.
ex.az: Mbps 是 bit 不是 byte；300 Mb ÷ 8 = 37.5 MB。

code.src:
mbps = 5
seconds = 2 * 3600
megabits = mbps * seconds
megabytes = megabits / 8
print(megabits, "Mb")
print(megabytes, "MB =", megabytes / 1000, "GB")

notes.t: print MB and GB (1 GB = 1000 MB)

demo.src:
# Try other values: change bitrate and minutes
mbps = 8          # e.g. 1080p
minutes = 30
mb = mbps * minutes * 60 / 8
print(round(mb), "MB used")

cards.tz: 低延迟模式与直播问题
cards.en:
Analogy: the buffer is a safety cushion. A thin cushion (low latency) lets you react fast but every bump hurts; a thick cushion (normal latency) is smooth but you're further behind.

Latency = delay between something happening at the streamer and the viewer seeing it. Live platforms offer a latency mode setting:

Low latencyNormal latency
Delaysmall, nearly real-timelarger
Buffersmalllarger
Smoothnessmore likely to stall on unstable networkssmoother
Best forstreamer replying to viewers' comments (gaming, Q&A)shows with no need for interaction

Before going live, consider: upload bandwidth, bitrate, formats and codecs, resolution, platform. Platforms may cap resolution (e.g. 1440p) in low-latency mode because high-resolution streaming requires higher bandwidth for buffering, so it is more likely to have high latency.

Exam wording: Low latency mode lets viewers watch nearly in real time, suitable for interacting with viewers' comments, but the smaller buffer makes playback more likely to pause on an unstable network.
cards.zh:
比喻：缓冲是安全垫。薄垫（低延迟）反应快但一颠就痛；厚垫（一般延迟）平稳但落后多一点。

Latency 延迟：主播那边发生到观众看到的时间差。直播平台有延迟模式：

  • 低延迟：接近实时、缓冲少、网络不稳易卡；适合主播回应观众留言
  • 一般延迟：缓冲多、较流畅、延迟大；适合不需互动的节目

开直播前考虑：上传带宽、bitrate、格式与 codec、解像度、平台。低延迟模式会限制解像度（如 1440p），因为高解像度需更多带宽缓冲，较易高延迟。

Exam wording：Low latency mode: nearly real-time, suitable for replying to comments, but more likely to pause on unstable networks.

ex.q: Janice's video conference is pixelated and laggy. Suggest two reasons.
ex.a:
1. Her network bandwidth is low or the connection is unstable.
2. The video bitrate/resolution is too high for her bandwidth.
ex.az: 带宽低或不稳；bitrate／解像度太高。

ex.q: A gamer wants to answer viewers' questions live. Which latency mode and what is the trade-off?
ex.a:
1. Low latency – viewers see the game nearly in real time, so questions match what is happening.
2. Trade-off: smaller buffer → more stalling if viewers' or streamer's networks are unstable; may need lower resolution.
ex.az: 选低延迟，能实时回应；代价是缓冲少，网络不稳易卡，可能要降解像度。

ex.q: A streamer with 5 Mbps upload bandwidth sets 4K at 20 Mbps 'because higher is always better'. What happens and what should he do?
ex.a:
1. He cannot upload 20 Mb every second through a 5 Mbps link.
2. Viewers see high latency, pauses and pixelisation; the stream may drop.
3. Fix: lower the bitrate below upload bandwidth (e.g. 720p/1080p at ~3–4 Mbps).
ex.az: 上传带宽 5 Mbps 不够送 20 Mbps，会延迟、卡顿、马赛克；应把 bitrate 降到低于上传带宽。

demo.title: Low vs normal latency on a shaky network

frames.en: Streamer sends live video. Viewer A uses low latency (2 s buffer). Viewer B uses normal latency (10 s buffer).
frames.zh: A：低延迟（2 秒缓冲）；B：一般延迟（10 秒缓冲）。

frames.en: A viewer asks a question. A sees the streamer's answer ~2 s later; B sees it ~10 s later.
frames.zh: A 约 2 秒后看到回答；B 约 10 秒后。

frames.en: A's 2 s buffer runs out → video freezes. B still has 10 s buffered → keeps playing smoothly.
frames.zh: 网络断 5 秒：A 缓冲用完而卡住；B 仍流畅。

frames.en: Low latency = fast interaction, less smooth. Normal latency = smooth, more delay.
frames.zh: 低延迟：互动快、较易卡；一般延迟：流畅、延迟大。

sq.q: Eva does research for a presentation.

parts.q: Compare a search engine and an online database as sources.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Search engine: content contributed by anyone and can change anytime [1]; database: published content evaluated for accuracy by publishers, more reliable [1].

parts.q: Explain what SEO is and why the top search result may not be the best source.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
SEO improves a site's ranking/visibility in search results [1]; ranking reflects optimisation/ads, not accuracy [1].

parts.q: State TWO search filters she can use to find a free-to-use image.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Usage rights (Creative Commons) [1]; size / type / colour / publish date [1].

sq.q: A designer prepares media for a website.

parts.q: Recommend an image format for (i) product photos, (ii) a logo that must be sharp on all screens, (iii) a sticker with animation and transparency. Explain each.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
(i) JPG/WebP – small lossy files suitable for photos, compatible [2]; (ii) SVG – vector, scales without losing quality [2]; (iii) APNG/GIF/WebP – supports animation and transparency [2].

parts.q: Why should the site provide videos in both WebM and MP4?
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
WebM gives smaller files with similar quality [1]; browsers not supporting WebM can fall back to MP4 [1].

parts.q: A user's browser cannot display an AVIF image. Suggest TWO solutions.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Update the browser [1]; install a plug-in/extension or open with a supporting viewer/media player [1].

sq.q: A school plans to live-stream its talent show (90 minutes) at 6 Mbps.

parts.q: Explain what streaming is and the role of the buffer.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Media is delivered as a continuous flow so users play and download simultaneously [1]; the buffer stores loaded data ahead of playback so playback stays smooth when the network fluctuates [1].

parts.q: Calculate the data each viewer uses in MB (1 MB = 8 Mb). Show working.
State TWO technical factors to consider.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Upload bandwidth / bitrate / resolution / frame rate / codec and format (any two) [2].

parts.q: Should it use video conferencing or webcasting? Explain.
parts.ms:
Suggested answer:
Webcasting [1] – large/public audience, mainly one-way communication [1].

pr.task: Write data_mb(bitrate_mbps, minutes) that returns the data used (in MB, 1 MB = 8 Mb) when streaming at bitrate_mbps for minutes minutes, rounded to 1 decimal place.
pr.taskz: 写 data_mb(bitrate_mbps, minutes)，计算以该 bitrate 串流若干分钟的数据量（MB，1 MB = 8 Mb），四舍五入至 1 位小数。
pr.solution:
def data_mb(bitrate_mbps, minutes):
    return round(bitrate_mbps * minutes * 60 / 8, 1)
